findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively, the liability threshold is 90% (not 70%), damages are 100% of the nightly room rate (not 70% lost profit), the hotel's occupancy records are declared final and binding with an explicit waiver of Group's audit rights, and there is no rebooking credit provision.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively across the entire block with liability triggered only below 70% pickup, damages capped at 70% of lost profit on the net group rate, audit rights preserved, and damages credited back on a CD-client rebooking.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block of 680 room nights. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of Group's single confirmed net group rate ($289.00), calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation, and Group retains the right to audit occupancy records. After receipt of this payment, Hotel will not seek additional damages from Group related to the room block commitment. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, with shortfalls calculated by comparing actual rooms occupied to the block size on each night of the event period. Group shall be deemed in attrition if actual occupancy falls below the attrition threshold of ninety percent (90%) on any night.
findings.exposure_basis: Worst-case: 680 total room nights (170x4) at 100% of $289 rate if occupancy dropped to e.g. 70% cumulative vs CD's 70%-lost-profit-on-30%-shortfall standard; illustrative gap between 100% nightly-rate liability and 70%-of-net-rate cumulative liability on a 30% shortfall (204 rooms) = 204 x $289 x (100%-70%) ≈ $17,687 minimum differential, but true exposure could be far higher given night-by-night triggering at only 90%.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel's occupancy determination and damages calculation are declared 'final and binding,' and Group expressly waives all audit and inspection rights over the Hotel's occupancy records.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have audit rights and a formula-based, non-discretionary damages calculation.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request, Hotel will provide access to its occupancy records, registration cards, and room-by-room occupancy logs for audit and verification purposes, and Group retains the right to contest the Hotel's occupancy calculations.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's occupancy records, registration cards, and room-by-room occupancy logs shall not be open to Group for audit, verification, or inspection, and Group waives any right to independently verify the Hotel's calculations or to contest the Hotel's occupancy records on any basis.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 45 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's 21-day maximum, and reservations after cutoff revert to rack rate rather than the group rate for as long as the hotel sells to the public; unassigned rooms are released without consultation with Group.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, with the group rate honored post-cutoff for as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the public, and unassigned rooms released only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public. After consultation with Group, Hotel may offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the block committed for the National Association of Coastal Engineers event shall be accepted by the Hotel only when received on or before forty-five (45) days prior to the arrival date of April 12, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Name changes are treated as new reservations at prevailing rate rather than honored at group rate; no-shows result in cancellation of the entire remaining reservation rather than reinstatement for the following night; individual cancellations are only free until 72 hours prior to arrival rather than 6 pm day of arrival; there is no provision crediting individual cancellation money against Group's attrition damages.
findings.cd_standard: Name changes should be allowed at the group rate up to arrival; no-shows should be reinstated for the following night; individual cancellation should be free until 6 pm day of arrival (or 24 hours before, with medical/personal emergency waiver); individual cancellation money retained by hotel should be credited against Group's attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. An attendee who fails to arrive on the first night shall be reinstated for the following night at the same rate unless Group directs otherwise. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.
findings.quoted_text: A name change on any individual reservation shall be treated as a new reservation at the Hotel's prevailing rate for comparable accommodations on the relevant dates, and the attendee shall be responsible for any rate difference between the Group rate and the prevailing rate.

findings.finding_text: Liquidated damages are calculated on gross room revenue for the full block (not 70% lost-profit on net group rate less allowable attrition), the hotel has no obligation to mitigate by reselling canceled rooms (resale revenue is expressly retained without credit), there is no rebooking credit, and the scale reaches 100% at 30 days or fewer with no liability-free window at all — even immediately after signing.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a disclosed sliding scale calculated against 70% lost room profit on the net group rate less allowable attrition, with an affirmative resale/mitigation duty crediting proceeds, and a rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit (defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $289.00) multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition, on the disclosed sliding scale. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and function space and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned by the Hotel for all guest rooms for all nights within the event period of April 12-16, 2027, based upon the negotiated room rate and the full room block size.
findings.exposure_basis: Full block gross revenue exposure at 100% tier: 680 room-nights x $289.00 = $196,520 gross; CD standard (70% of net rate, less attrition, with resale credit) would produce materially lower exposure — full gross-revenue-based 100% liability nearly doubles calculated lost-profit exposure of $137,564 (680 x $289 x 0.70).

findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation to attempt resale of released inventory, retains all resale revenue with no credit against Group's damages, and Group's records access and any mitigation-failure claim are expressly waived.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled rooms/functions and credit proceeds against damages owed, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, documenting its marketing efforts through all group and transient channels, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group. Records relating to mitigation efforts will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of any room inventory or function space by Group, whether through attrition, cancellation, or other reduction of Group's commitment, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory or function space, nor shall the Hotel be required to undertake any specific actions, marketing efforts, or promotional activities directed toward filling released space.

findings.finding_text: If the Hotel wrongfully cancels, Group's exclusive remedy is a refund of deposits only, with an explicit exclusion of consequential, incidental, and indirect damages, and Group bears its own attorney's fees regardless of outcome.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe Group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, including staff time, rate/airfare differentials, function space rental, and attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and telephone, postage, and printing costs.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel's sole obligation and the Group's exclusive remedy shall be the refund of any deposits paid by the Group to the Hotel, without interest and without liability for any other costs, losses, or damages incurred by the Group in connection with the event.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure is narrowly limited to objective physical impossibility and explicitly excludes epidemics, pandemics, public health emergencies, and government travel restrictions/advisories; there is no 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger, no waiver of fees for a reduced-size event, and deposits are forfeited rather than refunded — the clause states the Hotel retains deposits despite termination.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should allow cancellation for commercial impracticability, inadvisability (including health/safety), a 20%-or-greater attendee cancellation/anticipated cancellation, and should explicitly cover terrorism, disease/epidemics, government advisories and travel restrictions; deposits should be refunded promptly.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including acts of God, war, curtailment of transportation, strikes, threats or acts of terrorism, disease or epidemic, a CDC or governmental travel advisory, government closure, declaration of emergency, or government/corporate/educational travel restrictions — in that party's reasonable judgment make performance commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), illegal, or impossible, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that 20% or more of attendees will cancel. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, the following shall not constitute force majeure: government-issued travel restrictions, travel advisories, or governmental directives limiting group gatherings or travel, regardless of the reason such restrictions or advisories are issued; epidemics, pandemics, or declarations of public health emergency, including any government responses thereto; or concerns among Group members regarding attendee safety, willingness to travel, or health considerations.

findings.finding_text: Group forfeits its full deposit upon invoking the named storm cancellation right, with no refund unless a reschedule occurs.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation under a named-storm clause should be without liability; the standards library's model contemplates no-liability cancellation without deposit forfeiture.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Hotel will refund Group's deposit in full within five (5) business days, with no forfeiture.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Group shall forfeit the deposit paid to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel as partial compensation for the Hotel's lost revenue and costs incurred in preparation for the event.

findings.finding_text: Termination for the Hotel's uncured material breach still leaves Group liable for the Hotel's lost profits and consequential damages, and separately every termination — for cause or otherwise — is deemed a cancellation subject to the full liquidated-damages scale, eliminating any no-liability termination right entirely.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should let Group walk away with no liability and a prompt refund, entirely separate from and without triggering the cancellation clause's liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon Hotel's uncured material breach following thirty (30) days' written notice. Termination under this clause does not trigger the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the grounds upon which Group effects termination, whether for cause, convenience, or otherwise, any and all termination by Group shall be deemed and treated as a cancellation subject to the cancellation damages scale set forth in this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Shortfall is billed at 100% of the difference between the minimum and actual F&B revenue rather than a fraction (CD standard is 35%), and there is no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Any shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, not dollar-for-dollar, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: If Group's actual food and beverage consumption during the Event Period falls short of the minimum guarantee, Group shall pay the shortfall in full.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are used interchangeably with no separate definition or disclosed percentages for each, the Hotel has sole discretion over distribution with no guarantee that any portion reaches staff, and the combined 24% charge is applied to room charges as well as F&B (not carved out from room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee).
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined with both percentages stated; gratuity should be fully distributed to staff, while a separate service charge is disclosed as hotel revenue; neither should apply to room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: [X]% of the food and beverage total will be added as a gratuity and fully distributed to servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of [X]% is retained by Hotel as its own revenue and is not distributed as a tip. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement. Hotel will not add a gratuity or service charge to room charges, meeting room rental fees, or rented equipment that already carries a labor fee.
findings.quoted_text: A service charge and gratuity shall be added to all food and beverage, banquet, and room charges, and the terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' shall be used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and are not separately defined. The combined gratuity and service charge shall be automatically applied at the rate of twenty-four percent (24%) of the subtotal of all covered charges before tax.

findings.finding_text: There are no guaranteed minimum staffing ratios for servers or bartenders, staffing is entirely at the Hotel's discretion and non-challengeable, and labor/bartender fees apply to all functions rather than only those under 25 people.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server and bartender staffing ratios with no labor fee for meeting those ratios, and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide at least one bartender per seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one per one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender fees. No special labor or service fees will apply to Group functions except those under twenty-five (25) people.
findings.quoted_text: Staffing at food and beverage functions, including the assignment of servers, bartenders, runners, and other service personnel, is at the Hotel's discretion and shall be determined by the Hotel based on the number of attendees, the complexity of the menu, the duration of the function, and the Hotel's operational requirements.

findings.finding_text: No function room is named with square footage or ceiling height in the body of the agreement (Exhibit A lists space tentatively without square footage/ceiling height), the Hotel may reassign function space unilaterally by notice rather than requiring both parties' written consent, and meeting space rental is charged rather than waived, with no complimentary microphone/podium/power/lighting/HVAC commitment.
findings.cd_standard: Function space should be named with minimum square footage and ceiling height, reassignable only by mutual written consent, provided complimentary with rental waived, and each room should include a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the function space set out in Exhibit A, specifying minimum square footage and ceiling height for each room, with room rental charges waived. No change will be made to function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, lighting, and HVAC.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall assign all function space for the Group's use during the Event at the Hotel's sole discretion, and no function room is named or reserved in this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: AV and internet pricing is not locked at contracting and is subject to change up to the event, and complimentary internet/AV concessions are expressly conditioned on exclusive use of the Hotel's in-house AV provider, with forfeiture of internet access if Group uses an outside AV vendor.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV/internet quotes from contracting with at least 10 Mbps/1 Mbps bandwidth, and use of the in-house AV provider should never condition discounted or complimentary services like internet.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual and internet quotes prepared at the time of contracting, providing a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, including internet.
findings.quoted_text: Complimentary internet access and any discounted or complimentary services relating to audio-visual provision, including concessions, upgrades, or technical support at no charge, shall be conditioned upon the Group's exclusive use of the Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider for all function space during the Event.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose new fees at any time, even after signing, and Group waives any claim that undisclosed charges are unenforceable; a $35/night resort fee is applied to every room including complimentary rooms, with no waiver or discount for attendees.
findings.cd_standard: All charges must be disclosed in writing before signing; any undisclosed charge is waived; resort fees should be waived for attendees while resort-fee services are still honored.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including resort fees, surcharges, and any other fees. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Hotel will waive the resort fee for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee services.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose additional fees, surcharges, and service charges upon Group at any time, including without limitation after the execution of this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: $35/night resort fee x 680 total room nights = $23,800 over the event

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio is 1:75 rather than CD's 1:40, is described as a non-binding guideline the Hotel may reduce or withdraw at its sole discretion, complimentary rooms are still charged all fees/taxes/service charges/gratuities/resort fees, and complimentary room credits are entirely forfeited if occupancy falls below 100% of the block.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear, cumulative formula of one per 40 occupied room nights, not left to hotel discretion or forfeited due to attrition already compensated elsewhere.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. Complimentary rooms will not be subject to forfeiture based on attrition.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide complimentary room nights to Group based on a ratio of one (1) complimentary room per seventy-five (75) paid room nights occupied during the Event Period.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel retains an absolute right to sell rooms below Group's rate with no adjustment obligation for prior reservations, adjustments (if any) apply only prospectively and are treated as non-commissionable and excluded from pickup/attrition credit, and there is no 7-day-either-side rate ceiling relative to other groups.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee no lower rate is sold during event dates; if it happens, the group's rate should be adjusted retroactively or all such rooms should count toward the block, with commission and pickup credit preserved; the group's rate should be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates. If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match. Commission will be paid on the contracted rate regardless of any rate adjustment, and such rooms remain creditable toward Group's pickup, complimentary-room credits, and attrition. Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains the absolute right to sell rooms to the general public at any rate, including rates below the rate offered to Group.

findings.finding_text: Group waives any right to dispute billed amounts after receipt of invoice (no real dispute window before finance charges apply), the finance charge on unpaid balances is 1.5% per month compounding (above CD's 1% cap), and required prepayment amounts where credit is not approved are entirely at the Hotel's discretion rather than a staged, defined schedule.
findings.cd_standard: Master account should be payable upon invoice with a genuine dispute window before finance charges apply; finance charges should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; if credit is denied, Group should pay on a defined staged deposit schedule.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. A finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to unpaid, undisputed balances. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: All invoiced charges to the master account shall be due in full upon presentation, and the Group waives any right to dispute or withhold payment of billed amounts after receipt of an invoice from the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit may be applied against attrition, F&B shortfalls, and cancellation penalties (commingled with unrelated charges), is held in the Hotel's general operating account without interest, and the refund window is 90 days rather than 30.
findings.cd_standard: A security deposit should be refundable within 30 days absent documented, itemized damage, and should not be commingled with or used to offset unrelated charges like attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit collected under this Agreement will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may apply the security deposit, or such portion thereof as necessary, against any attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damages to the Hotel's premises, incidental costs, outstanding room charges, service failures, cancellation penalties, or any other sum that the Group owes to the Hotel

findings.finding_text: Relocated guests bear their own cost, taxes, and resort fees at the substitute hotel; the Hotel bears no transportation costs; there is no upgrade or welcome amenity on return; no per-room-night rebate to Group; walked nights are excluded from pickup/commission entirely rather than credited; and there is no additional compensation threshold for large-scale walks.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive comparable-or-better accommodations, round-trip transportation, message forwarding, and an upgrade/welcome amenity on return at hotel expense; Group should receive a per-room-night rebate, pickup/commission credit, no attrition liability for walked nights, and additional compensation for walks of 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak night.
findings.proposed_language: For each displaced guest, Hotel will, at its own expense, provide comparable-or-better accommodations, round-trip transportation, message forwarding, and upon return an upgrade and welcome amenity. Hotel will credit Group's master account $[X] for each night a guest is relocated. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's pickup and remain commissionable, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any walked night. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) of the peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: Any booking made by the Hotel at an alternative hotel shall be confirmed in writing to the guest, and the guest shall bear all costs associated with such alternative accommodations, including but not limited to room rates, taxes, and resort fees charged by the substitute hotel.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel makes no representation regarding construction/renovation, has no obligation to disclose or provide notice, and Group has no right to terminate, claim damages, or request a rate reduction even if work materially interferes with the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent no current renovation plans affecting Group's space, commit to 30 days' notice of confirmed work with mitigation plan, and let Group terminate without liability if it determines the work will interfere with its event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or guarantee regarding the status, scope, timing, or impact of any construction, renovation, maintenance, or capital improvement work that may be planned, in progress, or completed during the dates of the Event or at any time during the term of this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Notice of a brand/management/ownership change may be given as late as 90 days before the change (versus 30 days required generally), Group has only 10 days to elect termination (rather than 30), and bankruptcy/foreclosure/receivership events are expressly excluded from any notice or termination right.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a change in brand, management, ownership, bankruptcy, or foreclosure, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, and Hotel will refund all deposits within five (5) days.
findings.location_section: 23. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall provide such notice no later than ninety (90) days prior to the effective date of any such change, to the extent practicable and permitted by the Hotel's corporate counsel and applicable law

findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation to disclose collective bargaining expiration dates or notify Group of labor disputes, and Group has no cancellation right at all for a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract, however close to the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of disputes; if a strike/lockout/expired contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days of becoming aware of any labor dispute. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, or a strike, picketing, or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability.
findings.quoted_text: In the event of a labor dispute, strike, work stoppage, lockout, labor action, or other labor-related event affecting the Hotel or its operations, no cancellation window or notice period is defined herein, and the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement based upon the occurrence or threatened occurrence of any such labor-related event.

findings.finding_text: Group is required to use only Hotel-appointed vendors for all services, with a $2,500 surcharge per engagement for any unauthorized outside vendor.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge; in-house vendors should not be mandatory.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group's use of any outside vendor in violation of this requirement shall incur a surcharge of $2,500.00 for each such engagement.
findings.exposure_basis: Stated per-engagement surcharge for using an outside vendor

findings.finding_text: Indemnification runs one-way from Group to Hotel and explicitly extends to the Hotel's own negligence (carved out only for the Hotel's gross negligence/willful misconduct); the Hotel expressly disclaims any indemnification obligation to Group.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct; the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against all claims, losses, or damages, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party, its employees, agents, or contractors. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence. This provision survives termination or expiration of this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises, provided that Group's indemnity shall not extend to claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any warranty of ADA compliance and places all responsibility (including funding of auxiliary aids anywhere in the Hotel, not just Group's function space) on Group.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation, with each party funding auxiliary aids for its own areas (Group for function space, Hotel for guest rooms/common areas).
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the ADA. Group is responsible for auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, or any state or local accessibility law, and Group assumes sole responsibility for assessing the suitability of the Hotel's premises for Group's attendees and event purposes.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel's nondiscrimination obligations are limited strictly to what applicable law requires, with no voluntary commitment, and Group has no right to terminate if state/local law changes to permit discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on enumerated grounds even where law would allow it, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if state/local law changes to permit such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or marital, family, or military status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city adopt legislation affirmatively allowing such discrimination, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.
findings.quoted_text: In the event that any change, amendment, or new enactment of state or local law relating to discrimination, equal treatment, or the provision of services occurs after the date of this Agreement and before or during the Event, the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement, terminate the group block, reduce the room block commitment, or claim any modification to the terms hereof.

findings.finding_text: Attendee data may be used by the Hotel for its own marketing purposes and shared with affiliates and third-party marketers without further Group consent.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold/shared with third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: Group acknowledges that the Hotel may utilize such attendee data for the Hotel's own marketing, promotional, and business development purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email marketing, targeted advertising, and future event solicitation directed to attendees or their affiliated organizations.

findings.finding_text: Pickup reports are provided only upon Group's request rather than on a weekly schedule, the post-event report is due within 90 days rather than 30, and Group has no audit right at all over the Hotel's room block records — expressly waived.
findings.cd_standard: Group should get weekly pickup reports before cutoff, a post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost room-block audit right comparing the hotel's guest list against Group's registration list.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting [X] days prior to the cutoff date. Within thirty (30) days of departure, Hotel will provide a full post-event report. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with Group or independently by a ConferenceDirect or Group representative.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or verify the Hotel's room block records, reservation systems, or internal accounting related to Group's event, and Group waives any audit rights it might otherwise possess under applicable law or contract principles.

findings.finding_text: Assignment to a successor management company or affiliated entity requires the Hotel's consent, which may be withheld in the Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason or no reason at all, with no carve-out for a successor association management company.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are fixed to Maryland (the Hotel's location, not Group's), punitive damages are expressly available to the Hotel, and the prevailing party (deemed the Hotel if it recovers any material relief) may recover attorney's fees rather than each party bearing its own.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and venue should be the state/city where Group is located, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved controversy will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will be responsible for its own attorney's fees and expenses.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no commission clause at all providing for payment of ConferenceDirect's commission on room revenue.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, including rooms outside the block, miscoded rooms, walked rooms, and cancellation damages collected, within 30 days of departure.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement locks in a single confirmed rate for the entire event with no future-year rate escalation, so a future rate cap clause is not applicable here as drafted; however, no protection exists against subsequent increases relative to market decline. Given rates are fixed, this is noted as a gap only insofar as no rate-decline protection exists should market rates fall before arrival.
findings.cd_standard: Where rates are not yet confirmed for a future year, any increase should be capped at 2% and the rate should decline with market average, fixed no later than 12 months out.
findings.proposed_language: Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

analysis.document_notes: This is a heavily one-sided draft that departs from CD's standard position on nearly every major clause, with many clauses containing explicit Group waivers of rights (audit, dispute, mitigation claims) rather than the neutral or ambiguous silence typically seen. The 'facilities_services' clause type (service/facility reduction remedy) does not appear anywhere in the contract and is recorded as a missing clause is not separately itemized above because it overlaps substantially with the construction/renovation and reporting findings already flagged; treat the absence of any facility-reduction remedy as an open gap for the reviewing associate. Room block total used for exposure calculations: 170 rooms x 4 nights = 680 room nights at $289.00/night group rate. Signature blocks are unexecuted (no dates or names inserted)."

findings.finding_text: Attrition liability is triggered at 75% pickup (not 70%) and damages are calculated as 100% of the room rate for unoccupied rooms multiplied by 70%, but applied against the 90-room block minimum rather than the model's lesser-of formula comparing actual unsold hotel rooms. Also, the contract disputes deadline for attrition calculations is 30 days after final invoice, and there is no credit for rebooking after this Agreement's own attrition (only cancellation damages reference rebooking credit) — the attrition clause itself lacks a rebooking credit provision, and there is no cross-credit between F&B minimum overage and attrition shortfall.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should trigger only below 70% of the block, calculated as the lesser of unsold hotel rooms or shortfall, with a rebooking credit and F&B/attrition cross-credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block of 90 rooms. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate, calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of committed rooms, Group shall pay the Hotel liquidated damages equal to the room rate applicable to the unoccupied rooms, multiplied by seventy percent (70%), for each night the threshold is not met.
findings.exposure_basis: Difference between 70% and 75% threshold: 5% of 90 rooms = 4.5 rooms x $199 x 70% x 4 nights potential exposure gap; illustrative calculation of shifted threshold impact

findings.finding_text: The cancellation liquidated damages table imposes materially higher percentages than CD's standard sliding scale and reaches 100%-equivalent tiers far earlier than the model position. At the 364-181 day tier, damages are 35% versus a lower expected figure at that range, and by 180-91 days damages reach 52%, by 90-31 days 63%, and inside 30 days 70% — note the body text describing 0/25/50/75/100% conflicts internally with the table showing 0/35/52/63/70%, creating ambiguity, but on either reading the tiers assess damages well before the 12-month mark and at higher percentages at the near-term end than a typical scale reaching only 70% cap. Additionally, there's no explicit rebooking credit clause specific to cancellation matching CD's 100% rebooking credit language (the contract only credits future rebooking within 12 months, which is shorter than CD's suggested multi-year window), and the internal inconsistency between prose and table is itself a defect.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a disclosed sliding scale calculated at 70% of lost room profit, with mitigation duty, rebooking credit, and no punitive damages.
findings.proposed_language: Reconcile the internal inconsistency between the prose sliding scale (0/25/50/75/100%) and the table (0/35/52/63/70%) so a single, consistent schedule governs. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years of the cancellation, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text:
| 364 through 181 days prior to arrival  | 35%  |
| 180 through 91 days prior to arrival  | 52%  |
| 90 through 31 days prior to arrival  | 63%  |
| 30 days or fewer prior to arrival  | 70%  |

findings.finding_text: The shortfall penalty is a 35% surcharge added on top of the full shortfall amount ('the shortfall rate shall apply to any shortfall amount, assessed at thirty-five percent (35%) in addition to the base shortfall'), meaning Group pays 100% of the shortfall plus an additional 35% penalty — this is more punitive than CD's standard of paying only 35% of the shortfall instead of the full amount. There is also no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Any F&B shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, not the full difference, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall plus any additional surcharge. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The shortfall rate shall apply to any shortfall amount, assessed at thirty-five percent (35%) in addition to the base shortfall.
findings.exposure_basis: Cannot calculate exact exposure without knowing actual F&B revenue shortfall amount

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 35 days prior to arrival, which is earlier than CD's standard maximum of 21 days, reducing the window during which attendees can book at the group rate through the Hotel's block process.
findings.cd_standard: The room block cutoff date should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms within the group block must be made on or before thirty-five (35) days prior to arrival.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary internet in guest rooms regardless of loyalty program status is not addressed anywhere in the complimentary rooms clause.
findings.cd_standard: Attendees should get complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty-program status.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.

findings.finding_text: The service charge percentage is disclosed at 22%, but the gratuity percentage itself is never stated numerically in the contract, leaving the actual gratuity rate undefined despite CD's standard requiring both percentages to be confirmed in writing.
findings.cd_standard: Both the gratuity percentage and the service charge percentage should be clearly and separately confirmed in the contract.
findings.proposed_language: Gratuity of [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account and fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event, in addition to the twenty-two percent (22%) service charge already disclosed.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall pay a service charge of twenty-two percent (22%) calculated on the subtotal of food and beverage charges before tax.

findings.finding_text: Auxiliary aid costs in function/event space are to be 'divided between Group and the Hotel' rather than following the standard division where Group funds auxiliary aids in its function space and Hotel funds those in guest rooms and common areas.
findings.cd_standard: Group should fund auxiliary aids in event space and the Hotel should fund those in guest rooms and common areas, rather than a shared/divided cost arrangement.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: The cost of any auxiliary aids or services requested by Group or its attendees, including but not limited to interpreters, transcription services, specialized audio equipment and accessible transportation, shall be divided between Group and the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: There is no explicit provision requiring the hotel to contact Group in advance of a walk, to walk Group's attendees only after transient guests and other groups, or to honor a do-not-walk list, and there is no additional compensation trigger if the hotel walks 10 or more guests or 10% or more of the peak-night block.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should contact the group in advance of any walk, walk the group's attendees only after transient guests and other groups, honor a do-not-walk list, and pay additional compensation if 10 or more guests or 10% of peak-night block are walked.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will contact Group in advance of any relocation, will not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked under any circumstances. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation beyond the $100 per-night credit already provided.

findings.finding_text: The block may be adjusted by up to 15% at each of three review dates, which exceeds a tighter cumulative percentage in some CD baselines, but more importantly the room-block audit right (comparing hotel's in-house guest list to registration list, crediting miscoded rooms) described in CD's standard is absent — only a 'final reconciliation report' and self-funded audit option are present, without the specific no-cost cross-reference audit mechanism or credit for miscoded/brand-associate-rate rooms.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have a no-cost room-block audit right comparing the hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list, with any miscoded room — including brand-associate or business rate bookings — credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a representative of Group or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system — including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates or through Internet distribution channels — will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.
findings.quoted_text: The Group shall have the right to audit the room block at its own expense or, if it elects to conduct the audit itself, at no cost to the Group.

findings.finding_text: The named storm clause requires Group to provide written notice within twelve (12) hours of an NWS warning, which is an unusually short and operationally difficult window compared to CD's model of a 72-hour forecast-based cancellation right without such a tight notice deadline for Group.
findings.cd_standard: Either party may cancel without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice when a named storm is forecast within 72 hours of an event date, without an onerous notice deadline.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, Group may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice to Hotel's Director of Sales given within a reasonable time after the National Weather Service issues its warning, and in no event less than seventy-two (72) hours before the event start.
findings.quoted_text: Group must provide written notice of cancellation to the Hotel's Director of Sales within twelve (12) hours of the National Weather Service's issuance of a hurricane or tropical storm warning for the Portland area.

findings.finding_text: The future rate cap clause applies only if Group books a room block with the Hotel 'in any calendar year following 2027' — this is fine, but the clause allows the Hotel 60 days' notice and Group only 30 days to decline, which is not itself a CD standard element, however more importantly there's no issue on the 2% cap itself; rather the rate-decline protection is tied to 'the Hotel's standard market survey' controlled solely by Hotel with no independent verification standard beyond Group's right to request documentation. This is a narrower verification mechanism than CD's standard but is a minor gap.
findings.cd_standard: Should market average rate for comparable hotels decline, the group rate should be reduced by the same percentage, with Group able to verify via documentation.
findings.proposed_language: Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage, as measured by an independently verifiable market rate index or comparable-hotel published rates, with supporting documentation provided to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: If market room rates for comparable accommodations in Portland decline before Group's arrival on June 2, 2027, the negotiated group rate shall be reduced by the same percentage as the market decline, as measured by the Hotel's standard market survey.

analysis.document_notes: The cancellation clause (Section 5) contains an internal inconsistency: the narrative text describes a sliding scale of 0/25/50/75/100% of lost room profit tied to specific month-based windows (12mo/9-12mo/6-9mo/3-6mo/<3mo), while the accompanying table lists a different scale of None/35%/52%/63%/70% tied to day-based windows (365/364-181/180-91/90-31/<30 days). These two schedules do not reconcile and it is unclear which governs. This ambiguity itself should be flagged to the property for correction regardless of the cancellation finding above. Section 2 (Attrition) references a 30-day post-invoice dispute window that is shorter than the audit/dispute windows described elsewhere in the document (e.g., 10 business days in Section 6), suggesting some inconsistency in dispute-period drafting throughout the contract.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, and liability is triggered whenever occupied rooms fall below 90% of the block on any given night (versus CD's 70% cumulative threshold). Damages are also charged at 90% of the nightly group rate rather than 70% lost profit on the net group rate, and only apply to rooms not released -- there is no audit-based cumulative reconciliation, no F&B/attrition offset, and no rebooking credit provision.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability, if any, should be calculated cumulatively (not night-by-night), triggered only if pickup falls below 70% of the total block, with damages of 70% lost profit on the single net group rate, a 95%-occupancy night credit, audit rights, and a rebooking credit against damages paid.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $168.00 (plus tax, if required by applicable law), calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and the Group's block commitment is deemed satisfied only to the extent that occupied rooms meet or exceed ninety percent (90%) of the rooms reserved for each night of the Event.
findings.exposure_basis: Difference between 90%-of-block night-by-night threshold (charged at 90% of $168 nightly rate) versus CD's 70%-cumulative-threshold/70%-lost-profit standard on a 95-room peak-night block: at minimum, the gap between a 90% and 70% pickup threshold across 95 rooms x 3 nights represents substantially higher exposure than CD's standard; illustrative calculation: 20% of 95 rooms x 3 nights x $168 x 90% charge rate = ~$9,676, though actual shortfall depends on real pickup.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated against gross room revenue rather than 70% lost room profit on the net group rate, and the hotel has no obligation to mitigate by reselling and crediting proceeds -- the contract explicitly states resold-room revenue is retained by Hotel with no credit applied. There is also no rebooking credit provision.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be calculated as a percentage of lost room profit (70% of single net group rate), with the hotel obligated to mitigate by reselling cancelled rooms and crediting proceeds, and damages credited back if a CD client later rebooks the hotel.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit on the stated sliding scale, with 100% of room profit defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $168.00 at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall owe liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled or reduced rooms, based on the nightly group rates in effect at the time of cancellation
findings.exposure_basis: Gross revenue basis vs. 70% lost-profit basis on 95 rooms x $168/night x 3 nights = $47,880 peak block value; the difference between charging on gross revenue versus 70% lost profit is roughly 30% of the block value at the highest cancellation tier (70%), i.e., 0.30 x $47,880 x 0.70 tier ≈ $10,055-$11,148 depending on tier applied.

findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly disclaims any duty to mitigate or credit resale revenue against cancellation damages, stating the Hotel retains resold-room revenue with no credit applied, and there is no documented mitigation process, no 30-day-post-event payment deferral tied to mitigation evidence, and no record access for Group to verify mitigation efforts.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell cancelled rooms/functions through all channels, crediting proceeds against damages owed, with damages not due until 30 days after the event and only upon evidence of the mitigation effort.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel will document in writing its efforts to market the dates proactively through all group and transient channels. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold. All Hotel records relating to mitigation will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Any revenue the Hotel generates by reselling rooms within the cancelled portion of the Group's block shall be retained by the Hotel with no credit applied against the Group's liquidated damages obligation.

findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause requires notice within five business days 'of the event or restriction,' which is far shorter than CD's standard allowing notice at any time before the event regardless of when the triggering condition arose. The clause also lacks the 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger, does not explicitly list terrorism/CDC advisories/travel restrictions as separately enumerated causes tied to an attendee-cancellation threshold, does not address the situation where Group holds a smaller/reduced event (waiver of attrition/F&B/rental fees, lowest available rate), and does not clarify that the right survives even if the condition was known at signing.
findings.cd_standard: Either party should be able to cancel without liability when a qualifying cause would, in its reasonable judgment, make performance illegal, impossible, impracticable, or inadvisable, or cause/lead Group to reasonably anticipate 20%+ attendee cancellations, with notice permitted at any time before the event, and with fee waivers if Group instead holds a reduced-size meeting.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group -- including epidemics, disease, government or CDC travel advisories, government closures, or travel restrictions -- in that party's reasonable judgment make performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel their attendance. Notice of cancellation may be given at any time before the Event, whether or not the circumstances remain in effect at the time of the Event, and Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition at signing. If Group elects to hold a reduced-size Event despite such circumstances, Hotel will waive any attrition, food and beverage minimum, and function space rental fees related to the reduced size, and will offer Group's attendees the lowest room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: The party seeking to invoke force majeure must provide written notice within five (5) business days of the event or restriction, accompanied by reasonable evidence of its occurrence and material impact on performance.

findings.finding_text: The termination-for-cause clause only addresses material breach by either party and does not give Group the independent right to terminate without liability for a labor dispute, material change in ownership/management/brand, renovation interference, facility/service reductions, unavailability of a dependent convention center/overflow hotels, or discriminatory state/local legislation.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability and receive a prompt refund for a defined list of causes beyond mutual breach -- including labor disputes, ownership/brand change, renovation interference, facility/service reductions, dependent-venue unavailability, and discriminatory legislation -- separate from the cancellation liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: In addition to termination for material breach, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) unavailability of any convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends; or (h) adoption of state or local legislation permitting discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: When either party terminates this agreement for cause — due to material breach by the other party that remains uncured for ten (10) business days after written notice — the breaching party shall have no right to make a claim for damages, and the terminating party shall receive prompt refund of all deposits.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing a change in the Hotel's brand, management company, or ownership, or bankruptcy/foreclosure, and no corresponding notice or termination right for Group.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel changes brand, management, or ownership -- or files for bankruptcy or foreclosure -- before the event, it should notify Group within 30 days, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice, with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) days of the notice of termination.

findings.finding_text: The security deposit is stated as zero dollars and otherwise conforms to CD's standard on refund timing and non-commingling, but as drafted the clause exists purely as a placeholder; if a deposit is later required, it should retain the 30-day refund and non-commingling terms already present. No deviation found in substance beyond noting this is a nominal/zero-dollar clause requiring no further exposure.
findings.cd_standard: Any security or damage deposit should be reasonable relative to event size, refundable within 30 days absent documented damage, and not commingled with unrelated charges like attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: No change required to the deposit amount; retain existing 30-day refund and non-commingling language should any deposit amount be added in future negotiations.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide to Hotel a security deposit in the amount of zero dollars, which deposit shall be held by Hotel to secure Group's performance under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no warranty of ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, or transportation, and no allocation of responsibility for auxiliary aids or ADA indemnification.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should warrant ADA compliance for its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services, with mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations, and a clear division of auxiliary-aid funding responsibility.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA. Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.

findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision requiring the Hotel to disclose collective bargaining agreement expiration dates in advance, to provide notice of a labor dispute, or to allow Group to cancel without liability if a strike, lockout, or expired union contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expiration dates and prompt notice of any labor dispute; if a strike, lockout, or expired union contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not define or disclose any gratuity or service charge percentage on food and beverage, and does not address distribution to staff versus retention by the Hotel, or whether gratuity/service charges apply to meeting room rental or equipment rentals with labor fees.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined with both percentages confirmed in the contract, with gratuity fully distributed to staff and service charge disclosed as hotel revenue; neither should apply to room rental or equipment rentals carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any service charge of [X]%, plus applicable tax, is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement. Hotel will not add a gratuity or service charge to meeting room rental fees or to any rented equipment that also carries a labor fee.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no representation regarding current or future renovation plans affecting Group's space, no notice requirement, and no termination right if renovation interferes with the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent it has no current renovation plans affecting Group's space, commit to 30 days' notice of any later-confirmed work with details and mitigation plan, and let Group terminate without liability if the work will interfere with its event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the construction or remodeling will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.

findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision addressing closure or limitation of hotel amenities (restaurants, spa, fitness, meeting space) or reduced staffing ratios, and no right for Group to cancel or renegotiate if such reductions are not remedied.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits facilities by more than 25% or materially reduces service staffing ratios, it should first offer equal alternatives; if no resolution within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity, or materially reduces guest-to-staff service ratios, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, or the parties may modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.finding_text: Rates in this contract are fixed for the single 2027 event, but there is no provision addressing a rate cap or market-decline discount for any future-year confirmation, nor a stated deadline to finalize rates. Given the contract covers only one event date, this is a lower-priority gap but still absent as CD's standard contemplates.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, the contract should cap any increase at 2% per year, lower the group rate if market or published rates decline, and fix final rates in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should any room rates in this Agreement remain unconfirmed as of twelve (12) months prior to arrival, Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over the rates quoted in this Agreement, and will discount the group rate by the same percentage should the market average rate for comparable hotels, or Hotel's own published rate, decline before arrival.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no nondiscrimination commitment regarding attendees, and no termination right if the state or city adopts legislation permitting discrimination against attendees.
