findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on listed protected grounds, with Group able to terminate without liability if state or local legislation later permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or family, marital, or military status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the State of Texas or the City of San Antonio adopt legislation that affirmatively allows such discrimination or prohibits local nondiscrimination measures, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address confirmation timelines, name changes, individual cancellation windows, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund terms.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations should go out within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival), name changes at the group rate up to arrival, individual cancellation without charge until 6 pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement for the following night, and refundable individual deposits with 3 working days' notice credited against Group's attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or two (2) business days if within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made at the group rate up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no minimum staffing guarantees for food and beverage functions (servers, bartenders) and no cap on labor fees for smaller functions.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum staffing ratios for servers and bartenders at plated and buffet meals and bars, with no labor/service fees for meeting those ratios and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no audio-visual or internet bandwidth quote, no minimum bandwidth guarantee, and no discount commitment for additional AV/internet needs.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV and internet bandwidth quotes (minimum 10 Mbps download / 1 Mbps upload), give a stated discount on later additions, and never condition discounted internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will provide internet bandwidth of a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of [X]% on any additional bandwidth needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: The contract has no room-block review schedule at 24/12 months out, no weekly pickup reporting, no post-event report requirement, and no room-block audit right against the Hotel's guest list.
findings.cd_standard: The room block should be reviewed in writing at ~24 and 12 months out with adjustment rights, weekly pickup reports before cutoff, a final pickup report within 10 days and full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost room-block audit right with miscoded rooms credited to Group's pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting thirty (30) days prior to the cutoff date, and final room pickup reports with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. Within thirty (30) days of departure, Hotel will provide a full post-event report including rooms actualized, food and beverage revenue recap, and outlet spend. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, and any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission provision for ConferenceDirect at all -- no percentage, no payment timeline, no treatment of miscoded/walked rooms or no-show fees, and no commission on cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure regardless of master account payment status, non-cancelable and non-transferable, surviving management/brand change, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no rate parity guarantee preventing the Hotel from selling rooms at a lower rate than Group's contracted rate during the event dates, and no protection ensuring Group's rate is no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee it won't sell rooms at a lower rate than Group's contracted rate (except qualified rates), with retroactive rate matching or full block-credit if it does, and guarantee Group's rate is no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate of $168.00 during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match. Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no walk/relocation provision at all -- no advance-contact requirement, no do-not-walk list, no comparable-or-better accommodation or transportation guarantee for walked guests, no per-room-night rebate, no pickup/commission credit, and no protection against attrition liability for walked nights.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should contact Group in advance of any walk, walk Group's attendees only after transient and other groups, honor a do-not-walk list, provide comparable-or-better accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, and a return upgrade/amenity, credit the group's master account per relocated room-night, credit the relocated night toward pickup/commission, impose no attrition liability for walked nights, and pay additional compensation for larger-scale walks.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate any member of Group holding a confirmed reservation, Hotel will contact Group in advance, will not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked under any circumstances. For each displaced guest, Hotel will, at its own expense, provide comparable or better accommodations, complimentary round-trip transportation, message forwarding, and an upgrade and welcome amenity upon return. Hotel will credit Group's master account $[X] for each night a guest is relocated. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is walked. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel is located in San Antonio, Texas, a hurricane-belt-adjacent market, and the contract has no separate named-storm clause with its own notice period and cancellation window distinct from the general force majeure provision.
findings.cd_standard: In coastal and hurricane-belt markets, a separate, narrower named-storm clause with its own notice period and cancellation window should supplement general force majeure language.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any Event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the Event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no restriction on the Hotel's use of rooming list or attendee data for its own marketing purposes or disclosure to third parties.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold to third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision allowing Group to assign the Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without the Hotel's consent.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, where the event itself is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not name specific function rooms, square footage, or ceiling height requirements, does not address room rental fees or waivers, and does not guarantee complimentary in-room A/V basics (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage and ceiling height, prohibit changes without written consent, provide meeting space complimentary with room rental waived, and include a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement in this Agreement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The food and beverage minimum provision permits the Hotel to adjust menu pricing after the initial 12-month lock with only 60 days' written notice, and does not state that F&B revenue from affiliate organizations or exhibitors counts toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock menu pricing no earlier than 12 months before the event, and revenue from affiliate organizations and exhibitors should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will be confirmed at [year] pricing, or established not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event, without subsequent adjustment. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: Menu pricing shall remain locked at the rate quoted by the Hotel for twelve (12) months from the date of this agreement, after which the Hotel may adjust pricing in writing with sixty (60) days' notice.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not specify an actual prepayment percentage for Group if credit is not approved (it merely references 'a stated percentage' in a separate proposal, undefined in this Agreement), and does not include CD's staged deposit schedule or an automatic-credit-extension fallback if the Hotel fails to send or follow up on a credit application.
findings.cd_standard: If credit is denied, Group should pay on a staged deposit schedule (25% within 14 business days of denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before the event), or a defined prepayment percentage as fallback; if the hotel never sends or follows up on a credit application, credit should be extended automatically.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application, or fails to send a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: If Group does not provide advance credit approval, Group shall remit prepayment equal to a stated percentage of the anticipated room and food and beverage charges, as specified in the Hotel's proposal to Group.

findings.finding_text: After the cutoff date, the contract states the group rate applies only 'if rooms in the block remain available' and warns the guest may be offered only 'standard rack rates,' rather than continuing the group rate as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the general public (or the same room type once the block sells out). There is also no provision for holding unassigned rooms on prepayment, refunding advance payments, or releasing rooms after consultation with Group to reduce attrition damages.
findings.cd_standard: After cutoff, attendees should still get the group rate for as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the general public (or the same room type once the block sells), rather than reverting to rack rate or a narrower space-available test; unassigned rooms should be held on prepayment, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public. After consultation with Group, Hotel may offer any unassigned rooms in Group's block to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: The availability of rooms and the continued application of the group rate are not guaranteed after the cutoff date, and the guest accepts the risk that only standard rack rates may be offered.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is a relatively short, single-event agreement (Oct 19-21, 2027) for a 95-peak-night room block at $168/night. Several clause families standard in CD's library (commission, walk/relocation, rate parity, ADA, labor disputes, nondiscrimination, construction/renovation, facilities/services, brand/ownership change, gratuity/service charge, function space specifics, AV/internet, banquet staffing, review/audit dates, named storm, attendee data handling, assignment) are entirely absent from the document rather than addressed with weaker terms — these are flagged as missing clauses rather than deviations from existing language. The governing law/venue and insurance/indemnification and mandatory fees and outside vendor clauses were reviewed and found to align with CD's standard position, so no findings were recorded for those. The hotel_cancellation clause is also absent, though it duplicates the missing brand_ownership_change and termination_rights gaps in effect; no separate finding is recorded for it since the standards library's hotel_cancellation clause type was checked and found not present, but note that with no findings text possible without duplicating other write-ups, it is called out here in document notes for completeness."

findings.finding_text: Attrition threshold is set at 75% of block (liability triggers below 75% pickup) rather than CD's standard 70% threshold, and the damages rate is 75% of average daily room rate rather than 70% of lost profit on the single net group rate. There is also no mention of crediting excess F&B revenue against attrition damages, no rebooking credit if a CD client rebooks the hotel, and no dollar-for-dollar netting between F&B overage and attrition.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should trigger only below 70% cumulative pickup, damages calculated at 70% lost profit on the single net group rate, with F&B/attrition dollar-for-dollar crediting and a rebooking credit for CD clients.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block, calculated cumulatively. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause.

findings.finding_text: The rooming list deadline/cutoff is set at 32 days prior to arrival, later than CD's maximum of 21 days out. Additionally, post-cutoff pricing is left to the hotel's 'yield management practices and current market conditions' rather than guaranteeing the group rate for as long as the hotel sells to the public or the same room type once the block sells out, and there is no provision for holding, prepaying, or releasing unassigned rooms in consultation with Group to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff date should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, with the group rate continuing post-cutoff as long as the hotel sells rooms to the public (or the same room type once the block sells out), and unassigned rooms handled via prepayment-hold, refund, or consultative release.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public. After consultation with Group, Hotel will offer any unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list containing all guest names, room type preferences, and arrival and departure dates no later than thirty-two (32) days prior to the Event's opening day.

findings.finding_text: The cancellation liability-free window is 12 months (365 days), and the sliding scale tiers (35%/52%/63%/70%) are steeper at every tier than CD's typical scale, without disclosure of the underlying dollar amount at each tier or confirmation the profit percentage (70%) is applied against the block less allowable attrition. There is no rebooking credit clause for a CD client rebooking after cancellation (only Group's own rebooking is credited), and punitive damages language is only addressed in the governing law section, not tied specifically here.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale calculated at 70% of lost room profit on the single net group rate applied to the block less allowable attrition, with the dollar amount disclosed at each tier, hotel mitigation duty, and a rebooking credit extending to any ConferenceDirect client (not just Group itself) rebooking within a defined period.
findings.proposed_language: Revise the cancellation schedule so that liquidated damages are calculated as a percentage of room profit (defined as 70% of the confirmed single net group rate multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition), disclose the dollar amount owed at each tier, and extend the rebooking credit to any ConferenceDirect client that rebooks the Hotel within two (2) years of cancellation, not solely Group.
findings.quoted_text: Cancellations occurring within the liability-free cancellation window of twelve (12) months shall be subject to the sliding scale set forth in Schedule A attached hereto.

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked 14 months prior to the event, exceeding CD's 12-month maximum. The shortfall penalty is 40% of the difference, above CD's benchmark of 35%. The clause is also silent on whether affiliate organization or exhibitor F&B revenue counts toward the minimum, and gives the Hotel unilateral discretion to negotiate or waive the shortfall (a one-sided discretion that doesn't protect Group's own position).
findings.cd_standard: Menu pricing should be locked no earlier than 12 months prior to the event; shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap; affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will be established not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not forty percent (40%). Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal at least fourteen (14) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked and shall not be subject to increase or modification after that date.

findings.finding_text: The clause states both gratuity and service charge will be added, but does not confirm that the gratuity/service charge will not be applied to meeting room rental fees or rented equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.cd_standard: Neither gratuity nor service charge should be added to meeting room rental or to equipment rentals that already carry a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will not add a gratuity or service charge to meeting room rental fees or to any rented equipment that also carries a labor fee.
findings.quoted_text: Charges for food, beverage, and related services rendered to Group shall be subject to both a gratuity and a service charge, each calculated and applied separately according to the terms hereinafter set forth.

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio is set at 1 per 45 occupied room nights, which is less favorable than CD's benchmark of 1 per 40. The clause also doesn't address crediting no-show/cancellation fees as room nights toward the ratio, or complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned at one per 40 occupied room nights, with no-show/cancellation fee nights counted toward pickup, and complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block. Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup for purposes of this calculation. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio is forty-five (45), meaning that for every forty-five (45) paid room nights generated by Group, the Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room night at no charge to Group.

findings.finding_text: Although Group may use outside vendors, the contract imposes an outside vendor surcharge, contradicting CD's standard that no additional fee or surcharge should be charged for using an outside vendor. (The stated amount is currently $0.00, but the clause structurally reserves the Hotel's right to impose such a surcharge.)
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Delete the outside vendor surcharge provision entirely. Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, and transportation.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the Group's right to engage outside vendors, the Group shall remit to the Hotel an outside vendor surcharge in the amount of "$0.00".

findings.finding_text: The insurance obligation is imposed on Group alone, with no reciprocal requirement that the Hotel carry its own insurance to protect its activities, deviating from CD's standard of a mutual insurance obligation.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect their own respective activities against claims arising out of the Event. The Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of $2,500,000 per occurrence as set forth herein, naming Hotel as additional insured, and Hotel shall likewise maintain adequate liability insurance covering its own operations.
findings.quoted_text: The Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of "$2,500,000.00" per occurrence, covering bodily injury, property damage, and contractual liability arising out of the Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel's premises.

findings.finding_text: Auxiliary aid costs are to be divided between Group and Hotel via case-by-case negotiation, rather than the clear division CD calls for: Group funding aids in its function space, Hotel funding aids in guest rooms/common areas.
findings.cd_standard: A clear division of who funds auxiliary aids in event space (group) versus guest rooms and common areas (hotel), rather than an ad hoc negotiated split.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be divided between the Group and the Hotel... and the parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of costs for each specific auxiliary aid, with the Hotel bearing its proportionate share of expenses reasonably attributable to the Hotel's facilities or obligations under the Americans with Disabilities Act.

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are tied to the state where Group maintains its principal offices — this matches CD's standard for venue favoring Group's location. However, no finding is needed here as it already conforms; flagging is limited to confirm no deviation. [Correction: this entry mistakenly included; removing]
findings.cd_standard: N/A
findings.proposed_language: N/A

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on late undisputed balances is set at 1.3% per month, exceeding CD's cap of 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less. The invoice dispute window is only 12 days, shorter than CD's standard 30-day dispute window before finance charges accrue. If credit is not pre-approved, Group must prepay 75% of estimated charges in a lump sum rather than CD's staged schedule (25%/25%/50%) or a lower flat percentage.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on late, undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; Group should have a real dispute window (30 days) before charges accrue; if credit is denied, payment should follow a staged deposit schedule (25% at 14 business days after denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before event) rather than an open-ended lump-sum prepayment.
findings.proposed_language: Finance charges on any undisputed, unpaid invoice balance will not exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event, rather than a single 75% prepayment.
findings.quoted_text: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge of 1.3% on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date.

findings.finding_text: The annual rate increase cap is set at 3%, exceeding CD's standard cap of 2% per year. Also, rates are confirmed as final 11 months prior to the event, later than CD's 12-month deadline, and while a downward market adjustment provision exists, its trigger relies on the Hotel providing documentation and Group affirmatively electing in writing, rather than an automatic dollar-for-dollar adjustment.
findings.cd_standard: Room rate increases for future years should be capped at 2% per year; rates should be fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event; and the group rate should automatically decrease if the market/hotel's own published rate declines.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall not increase group room rates from year to year by more than two percent (2%) annually. Room rates will be confirmed as final in writing no later than twelve (12) months prior to the event dates. Should the market average rate for comparable hotels, or the Hotel's own published transient rate over the same pattern, decline before Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted automatically by the same percentage.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not increase the group room rates from year to year by more than three percent (3%) on an annual basis.

findings.finding_text: Commission is set at 9%, below CD's standard 10%. The remittance timeline is 35 days after the event, exceeding CD's 30-day standard. The clause also does not address commission on cancellation damages collected by the Hotel (CD standard calls for 10% of any liquidated damages paid to CD), nor does it include language that Group could not have negotiated better terms directly, nor address commission surviving a change of management/brand at a rate no less than what's contracted.
findings.cd_standard: Commission should be 10% of all actualized room revenue, paid within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable/non-transferable, surviving brand/management changes, plus 10% of any liquidated damages collected, with confirmation Group could not have negotiated better terms directly.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC, payable within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them. Should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission or the new brand's commission if higher.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall pay to Group a sales commission equal to nine percent (9%) of all room revenue actualized in connection with the Event, whether such rooms are booked as part of the blocked allocation or otherwise procured by Group members through independent channels.

findings.finding_text: Advance notice of collective bargaining agreement expirations is required only 9 months prior, short of CD's standard one-year notice. Additionally, the cancellation window for Group after becoming aware of a labor dispute is 75 days, which is much longer and vaguer than CD's requirement tying cancellation rights to disputes arising within 90 days of the event (this contract's structure ties the window to awareness rather than proximity to the event, which is a looser standard but the notice-period gap on CBA expirations remains a deviation).
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give one year's advance notice of CBA expirations, and Group should be able to cancel without liability if a strike, lockout, or expired contract with union employees arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, or no later than [date], Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, rather than nine (9) months.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than nine (9) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel's notice window for a change of brand, management, or ownership is 35 days following execution of the agreement (an odd fixed post-signing deadline) rather than 30 days of the change itself, and the Group's termination right is conditioned on 'demonstrating in good faith' that the change materially affects performance or alters service standards — an added burden not found in CD's standard, which grants termination at Group's discretion within 30 days of notice.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a brand/management/ownership change, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice, without needing to prove material impact.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of any material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or of bankruptcy filing or foreclosure. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, without need to demonstrate that the change materially affects Hotel's performance.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall notify the Group in writing of any change in the Hotel's brand affiliation, management company, or ownership within thirty-five (35) days following execution of this Agreement or, if such change occurs after that period, as promptly as commercially practicable and in no event later than the date any such change becomes effective.
findings.location_section: 21. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership

findings.finding_text: The threshold for triggering the Hotel's obligation to offer alternatives is a reduction of more than 30% of stated capacity or scope, above CD's standard threshold of 25%.
findings.cd_standard: The triggering threshold for facility/service reduction should be more than 25% of published capacity or offering, not 30%.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services.
findings.quoted_text: In the event that circumstances beyond the Hotel's reasonable control necessitate the temporary or permanent reduction, limitation, or discontinuation of any facility or service by more than thirty percent (30%) of its stated capacity or scope, the Hotel shall immediately notify Group in writing

findings.finding_text: The named storm cancellation window is 60 hours prior to the first event date, shorter than CD's standard 72-hour window.
findings.cd_standard: A named storm clause should provide a cancellation window of 72 hours prior to any event date.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within seventy-two (72) hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice.
findings.quoted_text: A named storm cancellation window of sixty (60) hours prior to the first event date shall apply, during which either party may cancel this Agreement without penalty if the named storm warning or advisory remains in effect for the scheduled dates

findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause covers many of CD's required triggers (terrorism, epidemics/pandemics, travel restrictions/advisories) but does not explicitly reference commercial impracticability being determined 'in that party's reasonable judgment,' nor does it explicitly state the right survives even for conditions known at signing, nor does it address the fallback where Group holds a smaller meeting instead (waiver of attrition/F&B/rental fees and lowest available rate) — this fallback provision is entirely absent.
findings.cd_standard: If Group holds a smaller meeting instead of invoking full cancellation, the hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate it offers anyone; the right to invoke force majeure should not be limited by knowledge of the condition at signing.
findings.proposed_language: Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition when this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances at reduced size, Hotel will waive any fees related to a reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Upon the occurrence of any such condition, the Hotel and Group shall cooperate in good faith to determine whether the event can proceed in modified form.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision for a 24-month and 12-month written review of the room block allowing Group to adjust the block up or down by a set percentage at the group rate, and no explicit no-cost room-block audit comparing the Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list with miscoded-room crediting.
findings.cd_standard: The room block should be reviewed in writing at approximately 24 and 12 months out, with Group able to adjust the block by a set percentage each time; Group should also have a no-cost audit right comparing in-house guest lists against Group's registration list, with miscoded rooms credited regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing 24 months and again 12 months prior to arrival. At Group's discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to 10% at each review, at the group rate. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, and any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid.

findings.finding_text: The rate parity clause applies only during the exact event dates (Nov 9-12, 2027) and does not extend 7 days on either side of the event as CD's standard calls for.
findings.cd_standard: The group's rate should be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates of November 9-12, 2027.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel agrees that during the Event dates of November 9 through November 12, 2027, the Hotel shall not advertise, offer, book, or sell any room accommodations to the general public, any individual guest, any tour operator, any travel agent, any online travel agency, any corporate account, or any other third party at a nightly rate lower than the rate extended to the Institute of Certified Actuarial Analysts under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause addressing audio-visual or internet bandwidth quotes, discounts on additional AV/internet needs, or a guarantee that use of the in-house AV provider is not a condition for discounted or complimentary internet service.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor AV and internet bandwidth quotes attached at contracting (minimum 10 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload), give a stated discount on later additions, and never condition discounted or complimentary internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will provide internet bandwidth of at least 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload, with a discount on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision guaranteeing minimum staffing ratios for servers or bartenders at food and beverage functions, or a cap on labor fees for small functions.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum staffing at food and beverage functions (one server per 25/20 guests for plated meals, one per 40/30 for buffets, one bartender per 75/100 guests) with no extra labor or service fee for meeting these ratios, and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address individual reservation confirmation timelines, name changes at the group rate, individual room cancellation deadlines (6pm day of arrival), no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing and crediting of retained cancellation money against Group's attrition damages.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation handling should include prompt confirmations, name changes at group rate up to arrival, cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement for the following night, and individual cancellation money credited against Group's attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation within four (4) days, or two (2) business days within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made at the group rate up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation. Any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The mandatory fees clause achieves disclosure and waiver of undisclosed fees and waives the resort fee, but it does not address early check-in fees or checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in or departing after check-out.
findings.cd_standard: Attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel charges no resort fee to Group for room accommodations during the Event, and no per-room resort fee, destination fee, facility charge, or similar daily room surcharge shall be applied to any guest room occupied by Group members.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause naming specific function rooms, their minimum square footage or ceiling heights, no restriction against the Hotel changing space assignments without written consent, and no guarantee of complimentary meeting space with waived rental or complimentary in-room equipment (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room, with its minimum square footage and ceiling height, restrict changes without both parties' written consent, waive room rental for space in the program agenda, and provide a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge in each meeting room.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Group's program agenda, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement in this Agreement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no nondiscrimination clause protecting attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity, race, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or similar grounds, nor a termination right if state or local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds, with a termination right if state/local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state of New York or the city of New York adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: The relocation clause omits several protections: there is no requirement that the Hotel contact Group in advance of a walk, no priority protecting Group members from being walked before transient guests and other groups, no do-not-walk list for key attendees, and no additional compensation obligation if 10 or more guests or 10% or more of the peak-night block are walked. It also lacks a per-room-night rebate credit to Group's master account for each relocated guest.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should contact the group in advance of any walk, walk the group's attendees only after transient guests and other groups, honor a do-not-walk list, provide a per-room-night rebate to Group, and pay additional compensation if 10 or more guests or 10% or more of the peak-night block are walked.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will contact Group in advance of any walk, will not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked under any circumstances. Hotel will credit Group's master account $[X] for each night a guest is relocated, regardless of that guest's rate. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: In the event that the Hotel is unable to honor all guaranteed reservations due to overbooking or operational circumstance, the Hotel shall relocate any affected guest to comparable or better accommodations at a Hotel property or an alternative establishment at the Hotel's sole cost and expense.

findings.finding_text: The resale/mitigation duty is described but cancellation damages are due within 30 days of receiving Group's cancellation notice (per Section 4), rather than 30 days after the meeting dates as CD's standard specifies, and there is no explicit condition that damages are contingent on Hotel showing evidence that mitigation occurred and the rooms went unsold before payment is due.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should not fall due until 30 days after the meeting dates, and only once the hotel shows reasonable evidence of its mitigation effort and that the rooms and space it held went unsold.
findings.proposed_language: Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates (rather than thirty (30) days after receiving Group's cancellation notice), provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall calculate the final damages due within thirty (30) days of receiving Group's cancellation notice and shall provide Group with a written accounting that itemizes the damages calculation, resale credits applied, and any remaining amount due.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is a fairly complete, well-structured Group Sales Agreement with numbered sections roughly tracking most of CD's standard clause categories, plus a referenced 'Schedule A' cancellation sliding-scale table not included in the excerpt (dollar amounts by tier are not disclosed beyond percentages). No exhibits, riders, or signature dates were provided, and several clause categories in CD's standards library (function space specs, banquet staffing ratios, AV/internet quotes, reservation procedures for individual guests, room-block review dates, and nondiscrimination) are entirely absent from the document rather than merely non-conforming. One finding (governing_law_venue) was drafted in error as a non-finding and should be disregarded/removed since that clause conforms to CD's standard and is properly reflected only in clauses_checked."

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, the trigger threshold is 80% (not 70%), damages are calculated at 80% of the full nightly room rate (not 70% lost profit), Group gets no credit for a night unless the Hotel achieves 100% occupancy (CD standard is 95%), and Group is expressly denied any audit rights, with the Hotel's calculation deemed 'final and binding' with no formula-based verification, no rebooking credit, and no offset for excess F&B.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be measured cumulatively across the entire room block, triggered only below 70% pickup, damages capped at 70% lost profit on the single net group rate, with full credit for any night at 95%+ occupancy, group audit rights, and rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate ($189.00), calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation. After receipt of this payment, Hotel will not seek additional damages from Group related to the room block commitment. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within [X] years, Hotel will credit the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and Group's block commitment is calculated as the total number of room nights reserved under the block minus attrition, if any.
findings.exposure_basis: Per unoccupied room night: 80% of $189 group rate = $151.20/night vs. CD standard of 70% lost profit, applied without cumulative or 95%-occupancy credit protections.

findings.finding_text: The contract denies Group any right to inspect, audit, or challenge the Hotel's occupancy records, and makes the Hotel's damages calculation 'final and binding' with no formula-based verification.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have audit rights and a formula-based, not discretionary, damages calculation.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily occupancy report showing the information needed to verify the attrition calculation, and Group may dispute the Hotel's determination in good faith.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's calculation of attrition damages shall be final and binding on Group, and Group shall have no right to inspect, audit, or challenge the Hotel's occupancy records or the Hotel's determination of room nights sold, occupied, or available on any night during the Event.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 45 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's maximum of 21 days, and reservations after cutoff revert to rack rate rather than the group rate for as long as the hotel is selling to the public; no provision addresses unassigned rooms being held, refunded, or released to reduce attrition.
findings.cd_standard: The cutoff date should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, with attendees continuing to receive the group rate after cutoff for as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the public, and unassigned rooms handled to reduce Group's attrition exposure.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type. After consultation with Group, Hotel will offer any unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: All room reservations on behalf of Group must be requested and confirmed by the Hotel no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the Event check-in date of July 13, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than 70% lost profit, the Hotel has no mitigation obligation and expressly retains all resale proceeds without crediting Group, there is no rebooking credit, and the scale runs from 20% up to 80% with no liability-free window at all.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be calculated against lost room profit (70% of the single net group rate) on a disclosed sliding scale, with an affirmative mitigation/resale-crediting duty and rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate ($189.00) — multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition, on the sliding scale stated in Appendix A. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms and will credit those resale revenues against the cancellation damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should Group rebook the Hotel within [X] years, Hotel will credit the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled room nights.
findings.exposure_basis: Gross revenue basis (vs 70% lost-profit basis) across a 20%-80% sliding scale on 275 peak rooms at $189/night materially increases exposure, though full multi-night dollar figure is not calculable from the data given.

findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly states no liability-free cancellation window exists under any circumstances, and no punitive-damages limitation applies (in fact the governing law clause grants the Hotel punitive damages).
findings.cd_standard: Any award for breach should be limited to actual damages, with no punitive damages, and termination for cause should be a separate, no-liability path.
findings.proposed_language: Any award for breach of this Agreement is limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not apply. Termination for cause under Article 8 is a separate remedy that does not trigger the cancellation damages scale.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall not be relieved of its liability for liquidated damages by any cancellation by Group occurring on or after the date of signature of this Agreement, and no liability-free cancellation window or period shall exist under any circumstances.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation whatsoever to attempt to resell canceled/released rooms or function space, retains all resale proceeds without crediting Group, and denies Group any right to review resale records.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to try to resell canceled rooms/space and credit proceeds against damages owed, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled or released rooms and function space, documenting its marketing efforts through group and transient channels, and will credit resale revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel records relating to mitigation efforts will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of rooms or function space by Group, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory, and Group waives any right to require the Hotel to undertake resale efforts or to mitigate damages through the placement of such space with alternative guests or groups.

findings.finding_text: Government-imposed travel restrictions and government travel advisories are expressly excluded as qualifying force majeure events, contrary to CD's standard, and deposits/prepayments are retained by the Hotel entirely with no refund even where force majeure applies.
findings.cd_standard: Qualifying causes should explicitly include CDC and government travel advisories and government travel restrictions, and deposits should be refunded promptly upon a force majeure cancellation.
findings.proposed_language: Qualifying force majeure events include, without limitation, a CDC advisory, a State Department or other governmental or international agency travel advisory, and government, corporate, or educational institution travel restrictions. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination invoking force majeure.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither government-imposed travel restrictions nor government travel advisories of any kind, whether mandatory or advisory in character, shall be deemed a force majeure event excusing or limiting the obligations of Group under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Deposits and prepayments are retained by the Hotel in their entirety upon invocation of force majeure, with no refund to Group under any circumstances.
findings.cd_standard: Deposits should be refunded promptly when force majeure is invoked.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination invoking force majeure.
findings.quoted_text: Group's deposits and prepayments made to the Hotel shall be retained by the Hotel in their entirety, and Group shall have no claim against the Hotel for the return of any funds, whether characterized as deposits, prepayments, or advances, notwithstanding the invocation of force majeure.
findings.exposure_basis: Security deposit of $25,000 (Section 15) plus any additional prepayments could be forfeited entirely upon force majeure.

findings.finding_text: Any termination by Group, regardless of cause (including force majeure, labor disputes, brand change, etc.), is treated as a cancellation subject to the liquidated damages scale, and Group remains liable for additional damages beyond that scale at the Hotel's election.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause (including force majeure, labor disputes, brand change, renovation interference, facility reduction, and similar causes) should allow Group to walk away with no liability and should not trigger the cancellation clause's liquidated-damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon force majeure, a qualifying labor dispute, a material change in Hotel's ownership, management, or brand, interfering renovation, a reduction in Hotel facilities or services, or other causes recognized under this Agreement. None of the foregoing will trigger the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Any termination of this Agreement by the Group, irrespective of the cause or justification asserted by the Group, shall be treated as a cancellation by the Group under the cancellation damages scale set forth in Article 8, and the Group shall pay to the Hotel the cancellation damages calculated in accordance with that scale based on the date on which the termination notice is delivered.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing the Hotel's liability if the Hotel itself cancels the agreement without a contractual right to do so; instead the termination clause is entirely one-sided in the Hotel's favor.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a right to do so, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages arising from the cancellation.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.finding_text: The named storm clause requires the warning to remain in effect 24 hours before arrival and requires cancellation notice 24 hours before arrival, which is a narrower window than CD's standard 72-hour notice/cancellation window.
findings.cd_standard: A named storm clause should allow cancellation without liability when a named storm is forecast to affect the hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm, or equivalent) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within seventy-two (72) hours of any event date, Group may cancel the affected portion of the Event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.
findings.quoted_text: If the National Weather Service issues a named storm warning for the geographic area in which the Hotel is located at any time during the period commencing twenty-four (24) hours before the start of the Event and continuing through the final day of the Event

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked in for 24 months from signature, exceeding CD's 12-month maximum, and any shortfall requires Group to pay the full difference rather than 35% of the gap; there is also no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock in pricing no earlier than 12 months before the event, and shortfalls should be billed at 35% of the gap, with affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will be confirmed at pricing established not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the guaranteed minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's Event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide to the Group a menu and pricing proposal that shall remain binding as to pricing for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the date of this Agreement

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are treated as interchangeable and undefined, with the Hotel retaining sole discretion to keep the entire 24% charge as its own revenue rather than distributing gratuity to staff, and Group is not told what portion (if any) reaches service staff.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined and percentages confirmed in the contract, with gratuity fully distributed to staff and any separate service charge disclosed as hotel revenue rather than presented as a tip.
findings.proposed_language: A gratuity of [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account and fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of [X]%, plus applicable tax, is distinct from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' are used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and do not constitute separately defined charges.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel reserves the right to assess additional fees at any time after signing in its sole discretion, and Group remains liable for charges even if never disclosed prior to signature; a non-negotiable $35/night resort fee applies with no waiver or fee-services offering.
findings.cd_standard: All charges must be disclosed in writing before signature; any undisclosed charge should be waived; later add-ons require Group's written approval; resort fees should be waived for attendees while still honoring resort-fee services.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including facility fees, administrative costs, technology fees, and the resort fee. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Should Group require additional services after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will waive the $35.00 per-night resort fee for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee services.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel reserves the right to assess additional fees, surcharges, and service charges against Group's account at any time following execution of this Agreement, in Hotel's sole discretion.
findings.exposure_basis: Resort fee of $35/occupied room/night across up to 275 peak rooms for multiple nights represents unwaived recurring exposure.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary rooms are set at only 1 per 80 occupied rooms (vs. CD's 1 per 40), are described merely as something the Hotel 'shall consider' providing (not a commitment), are subject to full forfeiture for any pickup shortfall with no partial credit, and are entirely within Hotel's discretion to withhold.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear, cumulative formula (1 per 40 occupied room nights) regardless of whether the block was otherwise met, not left to hotel discretion or fully forfeited for attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. Complimentary room credit will not be forfeited due to a shortfall in pickup, but will instead be calculated proportionally based on actual room nights realized.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall consider providing complimentary guestroom accommodations to Group at a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every eighty (80) occupied rooms successfully billed during the Event, provided Group achieves full pickup of its contracted room block.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel may sell rooms below Group's rate without any obligation to adjust Group's rate retroactively or on a going-forward basis for the whole block, and any adjusted rate offered is expressly excluded from commission and pickup credit.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel sells rooms below the group's contracted rate, the group's rate should be adjusted (including retroactively) or all attendee rooms should count in the block regardless of rate, with commission and pickup credit preserved either way.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, except for qualified rates (government, airline, contracted corporate rates). If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees. Commission will be paid on the contracted rate regardless of any rate adjustment, and such rooms remain creditable toward Group's pickup, complimentary-room credits, and attrition.
findings.quoted_text: Any adjusted rate made available to Group following identification of a lower public rate shall be treated as a non-commissionable rate and shall not be credited toward Group's room block pickup, occupancy targets, or performance metrics for purposes of calculating complimentary rooms, rebates, or other volume-based benefits under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: There is no dispute window before finance charges apply ('no period in which Group may dispute a charge'), payment is due in just 15 days rather than upon a defined review period, and the finance charge is 1.5% per month compounded monthly, exceeding CD's 1% simple cap. The contract also does not address what happens if Hotel never sends a credit application (automatic credit extension) or a staged deposit schedule if credit is denied.
findings.cd_standard: Master account should be payable upon invoice with a real dispute window before finance charges apply, finance charges capped at 1% per month (or legal max, whichever is less), automatic credit extension if hotel fails to send a credit application, and a staged deposit schedule if credit is denied.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If payment of undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance. If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application or a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: All invoiced amounts shall be due and payable in full when due, with no period in which Group may dispute a charge. Invoices shall be submitted by Hotel to Group's designated billing contact within thirty (30) days following the Event, and payment shall be due within fifteen (15) days of invoice date.

findings.finding_text: The finance charge rate itself of 1.5% per month, compounded monthly, exceeds CD's cap of 1% per month simple interest.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on late, undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month, or the legal maximum, whichever is less.
findings.proposed_language: A finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance, not compounded.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have the right to charge a monthly finance charge of 1.5% on the outstanding balance, compounded monthly, until such amount is paid in full.

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit may be applied by the Hotel in its sole discretion against attrition charges, F&B shortfalls, and other unrelated charges, is refundable only within 90 days rather than 30, and Group cannot offset or contest damage claims before other invoices are paid.
findings.cd_standard: Any deposit should be refundable within a defined 30-day window absent documented, itemized damage, and should not be commingled with or used to offset unrelated charges like attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: The $25,000.00 security deposit will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the Event's conclusion unless Hotel provides Group with an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall apply the deposit, in its sole discretion, against attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damage to Hotel property, unpaid room charges, cancellation fees, or any other amounts owed by Group to Hotel under this Agreement or otherwise.
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit amount at risk of being applied to unrelated charges and held up to 90 days rather than 30.

findings.finding_text: Walked guests must arrange and pay for their own alternative lodging and transportation, receive no upgrade or welcome amenity upon return, and the relocated room night is expressly excluded from Group's pickup and commission calculation, with no rebate to Group and no additional compensation threshold for mass walks.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive hotel-arranged comparable-or-better accommodations, round-trip transportation, message forwarding, and an upgrade/welcome amenity on return; Group should receive a per-room-night rebate and full pickup/commission credit for the relocated night, with no attrition liability and additional compensation for large-scale walks.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate a guaranteed reservation, Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable or better hotel; (b) provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel; (c) forward the guest's messages, mail, and packages; and (d) upon return, provide an upgrade if available and a welcome amenity. Hotel will credit Group's master account for each night a guest is relocated, and each displaced room will be credited toward Group's pickup and remain commissionable at the group rate, with no attrition liability for any night a guest is walked. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: The affected guest shall bear full responsibility for all transportation costs to and from any alternative hotel arranged pursuant to a walk relocation.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel makes no representation about current or planned renovation, may commence work at any time including during the Event without any advance notice, and Group has no termination right or remedy for disruption whatsoever.
