findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent it has no current renovation plans affecting Group's space, commit to 30 days' written notice of confirmed work with a mitigation plan, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if the work will interfere with its event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and Hotel's mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have the right to commence renovation work at the Hotel at any time, including during the Event, without providing Group advance notice of any kind, and Group shall have no right to object to or restrict such work based on timing, noise, dust, disruption, or any other impact on Group's event or its attendees.

findings.finding_text: Notice of a brand/ownership/management change is given only 90 days before the change (not within 30 days after), Group must terminate within only 10 days of notice (shorter than CD's 30-day window), and bankruptcy/receivership/foreclosure events are entirely carved out from any notice or termination right.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a change in ownership, management, or brand (including bankruptcy or foreclosure), and Group should have 30 days from that notice to terminate without liability, with prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither bankruptcy, receivership, foreclosure, assignment for benefit of creditors, nor any other proceedings or event arising from the financial distress or insolvency of Hotel or its parent, affiliate, or operating company shall trigger any notice obligation or afford Group any right of termination, cancellation, or offset, and Group's obligations hereunder shall remain in full force and expect regardless of any such development.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation to provide advance notice of collective bargaining agreement expirations or labor disputes, and Group is denied any cancellation right for a labor dispute, strike, or lockout affecting the Hotel, regardless of timing.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of actual disputes; Group should be able to cancel with no liability if a strike, lockout, or expired contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, or a strike, lockout, or picketing occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, and any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have no obligation to provide Group with advance notice, periodic reports, or any information concerning the expiration dates, renewal status, or negotiation schedule of any collective bargaining agreement, labor agreement, or labor arrangement applicable to Hotel's employees or operations

findings.finding_text: Group must use only the Hotel's in-house or exclusively-appointed vendors for catering, AV, floral, entertainment, and other services, and using an outside vendor triggers a $2,500 per-vendor surcharge, with disputes decided solely by the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: The group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge for services like AV, floral, security, transportation, and similar.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, catering support, floral, entertainment, and transportation. Hotel's in-house or exclusively-appointed vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group's use of outside vendors not approved in advance by the Hotel shall be subject to a surcharge of $2,500.00 per outside vendor service or vendor category, which surcharge shall be assessed in addition to any other charges imposed under this Agreement
findings.exposure_basis: Surcharge of $2,500 per outside vendor category used without Hotel pre-approval.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification runs one-way from Group to Hotel, explicitly extends to claims arising from the Hotel's own ordinary and gross negligence (only excluding gross negligence/willful misconduct claims arising 'solely' from the Hotel), and the Hotel has no reciprocal indemnification or insurance obligation.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, and insurance should be a mutual obligation, with the group never indemnifying the hotel for the hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its respective officers, directors, employees, and agents against all claims, losses, or damages arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party, its employees, agents, or contractors. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence. Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Group's indemnity obligations extend to and include claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence, ordinary or gross, provided that Group shall not be obligated to indemnify the Hotel for claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: Auxiliary aid costs are shared with Group bearing 'incremental' or 'specialized' costs as determined by an undefined baseline, rather than the standard division of function-space aids to Group and guest-room/common-area aids to the Hotel, and undisclosed aids may be charged solely to Group at the Hotel's sole discretion.
findings.cd_standard: Group should fund auxiliary aids needed in function space it holds; the hotel should fund auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide baseline auxiliary aids that are considered standard for its operations, while Group shall bear responsibility for the incremental cost of specialized or unusual accommodations tailored specifically to the Event and its participants' particular needs

findings.finding_text: The Hotel may use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes and share it with affiliates and marketing partners without Group's consent.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should not be used by the hotel for its own marketing or sold/shared with third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations and performing this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email, and telephonic solicitation of the attendees who registered for the Event.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no 24-month/12-month room block review points, no weekly pickup reports, and expressly denies Group any right to audit or independently verify room block records, treating pickup reporting as a purely discretionary courtesy.
findings.cd_standard: The room block should be reviewed in writing at roughly 24 and 12 months out with adjustment rights, weekly pickup reports before cutoff, a final report within 10 days of departure, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right comparing hotel and registration lists.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing 24 months and 12 months prior to arrival, with Group able to adjust the block by up to [X]% at each review at the group rate. Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting [X] days prior to cutoff, and a final pickup report with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with Group or independently by a ConferenceDirect or Group representative, with any miscoded room credited to Group's pickup.
findings.quoted_text: Group may request pickup information from the Hotel at any time, provided that the Hotel shall furnish such reports at its sole discretion and convenience, and Group acknowledges that the provision of pickup information is a voluntary service not required under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Group is denied any right to audit, inspect, or independently verify room block records or engage a third-party auditor, with all determinations made solely by the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have a no-cost room-block audit right, run jointly or independently, comparing the hotel's guest list against Group's registration list, with miscoded rooms credited to Group regardless of rate.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a representative of Group or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or independently verify the room block records maintained by the Hotel, nor shall Group have any right to engage a third-party auditor or representative to examine the Hotel's reservation systems, registration records, or billing documentation.

findings.finding_text: Assignment to a successor management company or affiliated entity requires the Hotel's sole and absolute discretion consent, with no standard allowing assignment without consent where the event is substantially unchanged, and any unauthorized assignment is deemed a material breach entitling the Hotel to cancel the entire block.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, particularly where the event itself is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment or transfer shall be entirely within the Hotel's sole and absolute discretion, and the Hotel may withhold consent to an assignment for any reason whatsoever or for no reason stated.

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are fixed to the Hotel's location (Indiana/Marion County) rather than Group's location, the Hotel is entitled to recover punitive and exemplary damages in addition to actual damages, and attorney's fees run to whichever party prevails rather than each side bearing its own.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and venue should be the state and city where Group is located, with no punitive damages and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved controversy or claim will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will be responsible for its own attorney's fees and expenses.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall be entitled to recover punitive damages, exemplary damages, and all consequential and incidental damages available under applicable law, in addition to actual damages, in any action arising out of the Group's breach or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission provision for ConferenceDirect at all — no commissionable rate, no payment timing, no protection for miscoded/walked/audited rooms, and no commission on cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, including rooms outside the block, walked rooms, and audit-credited rooms, and 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: The room rate of $189.00 appears fixed for the single event year with no future-year rate provision at all, but since the standards library calls for a future rate cap and market-decline discount mechanism whenever future rates are not yet confirmed, and no such mechanism appears here despite this being a multi-year-style negotiation context, this protection is absent from the contract.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, the contract should cap any increase at 2% per year and lower Group's rate if market rates decline before arrival.
findings.proposed_language: Definite room rates are confirmed in writing in this Agreement. Should any rate for an unconfirmed future contract year be established after signing, Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over rates quoted, and should the market average rate for comparable hotels decline before Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address confirmation timing, name changes at group rate, individual cancellation windows, no-show reinstatement, or crediting of individual cancellation fees against Group's attrition liability.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation handling should favor attendees: prompt confirmations, name changes at group rate up to arrival, cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement, and crediting of individual cancellation money against Group's attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information. Name changes may be made at the group rate at any time up to the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation. Any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no minimum staffing ratios for servers or bartenders at food and beverage functions and no cap on labor/service fees for small functions.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server/bartender staffing ratios at F&B functions with no extra labor fee for meeting them, and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender fees.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not address audio-visual or internet bandwidth quotes, discounts on additions, or a prohibition on tying discounted internet to use of the in-house AV vendor.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor AV and internet bandwidth quotes attached at contracting (minimum 10 Mbps download/1 Mbps upload), give a discount on later additions, and not condition discounted internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of provider. Hotel will provide internet bandwidth of at least 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload, with a discount of [X]% on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: The contract does not name specific function rooms, square footage, or ceiling heights, does not address room rental waivers, and does not commit to complimentary in-room equipment (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage/ceiling height, waive room rental for program agenda space, and provide complimentary basic AV/power/HVAC in each meeting room.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to function space assignments without written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially limits restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, or reduces staffing ratios for key services.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits facilities/services by more than 25% or materially reduces staffing ratios, it should first offer equal alternatives, and Group should be able to cancel without liability if no resolution is reached within 30 days.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity, or materially reduces service staffing ratios, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no nondiscrimination commitment protecting attendees and no termination right if state or local legislation permits discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds, with Group able to terminate without liability if state/local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, gender identity or expression, age, race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, or parental, marital, or military status. Should the state of Indiana or the city of Indianapolis adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

analysis.document_notes: This is a heavily one-sided hotel-drafted agreement (Crossroads Convention Hotel / Interstate Freight Brokers Federation, July 13-16, 2027, Indianapolis, IN) with numerous provisions that expressly strip Group of audit rights, dispute rights, and mitigation protections across attrition, cancellation, resale, and reporting clauses. Several clause types the CD standards library calls for (commission, hotel_cancellation, banquet staffing, AV/internet, function space specifics, facilities/services reduction, nondiscrimination, reservation procedures, future rate cap) are entirely absent from the document rather than merely drafted unfavorably; these are flagged as missing clauses. Article numbering in the text is internally inconsistent (Section 4 cancellation table is referenced as 'Article 8' within Section 8's text, and Section 10 references 'Article 7' for taxes/service charge which does not exist as drafted) — flagging as a structural/drafting irregularity worth the reviewer's attention independent of the substantive findings above."

findings.finding_text: The shortfall payment is defined as 35% of Group's total room revenue for the Event, not 35% of the F&B shortfall itself. This decouples the penalty from the actual F&B minimum gap and could produce a payment far larger than the actual shortfall, effectively converting a modest F&B minimum protection into an uncapped room-revenue-linked penalty. There is also no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Any shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap between actual F&B revenue and the minimum (not tied to room revenue), and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual food and beverage revenue and the minimum, not tied to room revenue. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The shortfall shall be calculated as thirty-five percent (35%) of the Group's total room revenue for the Event period.

findings.finding_text: The contract mandates use of the Hotel's in-house/exclusive vendors for AV, telecom, floral, décor, and entertainment, and imposes a $3,200 surcharge per outside vendor if Group wants to use its own.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge; in-house vendors should not be mandatory.
findings.exposure_basis: Surcharge per outside vendor as stated in the contract
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, telecommunications, floral, décor, and entertainment. Hotel's in-house or exclusive vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage the Hotel's in-house vendors or vendors with whom the Hotel maintains exclusive appointments for all ancillary services required in connection with the Event, including but not limited to audiovisual services, telecommunications, floral arrangements, décor, and entertainment. Any request by Group to retain an outside vendor not approved by the Hotel in writing shall be subject to a surcharge of $3,200.00 per outside vendor, which surcharge shall be payable by Group to the Hotel within ten (10) days of invoice.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is cumulative with a 70% threshold and 70% lost-profit damages and 95%-occupancy-night credit, matching CD's core formula. However, damages are based on 'average daily room rate' rather than the group's single confirmed net group rate, and the payment is not stated to fully settle all room-block damages (no explicit statement that payment settles all claims), nor is there any cross-credit between F&B surplus and attrition, nor a rebooking credit for attrition damages specifically (only cancellation damages address rebooking).
findings.cd_standard: Damages should be 70% of lost profit on the group's single net group rate, payment should settle all room-block damages, excess F&B revenue should credit against attrition and vice versa, and a rebooking credit should apply to attrition damages paid.
findings.proposed_language: Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate (plus tax, if required by applicable law) for each unsold room night below the 70% threshold. After receipt of this payment, Hotel will not seek additional damages from Group related to the room block commitment. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within two (2) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall be liable for attrition damages at the rate of seventy percent (70%) of the average daily room rate for each committed room night falling short of the threshold.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure covers many qualifying causes and allows termination, but it does not include the 20%-attendee-cancellation-anticipation trigger, does not preserve Group's right to invoke it for conditions known at signing, and does not address the reduced-meeting fallback (waiver of attrition/F&B/rental fees and lowest-rate offer) if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling outright.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should include a 20%-of-attendees cancellation/anticipated-cancellation trigger, apply regardless of whether the condition was known at signing, and if Group holds a reduced meeting, Hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer its lowest rate.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Force majeure shall also apply where the triggering cause causes, or leads Group to reasonably anticipate, cancellation by twenty percent (20%) or more of Group's attendees. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition at the time this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances at reduced size, Hotel will waive any fees related to a reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.'
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events shall also include conditions that render it unsafe or imprudent for meeting attendees to travel to or gather at the Hotel, whether due to health risks, infrastructure damage, or other circumstances beyond the parties' reasonable control.

findings.finding_text: The mandatory fees clause requires disclosure before signature and waives undisclosed charges, matching most of CD's position, but there is no waiver of resort fees for attendees (though the Hotel states it charges none, that is a fact not a commitment going forward), no provision on early check-in fees, and no waiver of checked-bag fees for attendees arriving early or departing late.
findings.cd_standard: Attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees, and where a resort fee exists it should be waived while services are honored.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.'
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel charges no resort fee for rooms reserved under this Agreement. All mandatory fees have been disclosed above, and Group's room rate is inclusive of all fees except those specifically stated in the written disclosure delivered before execution.

findings.finding_text: There is no 24-month/12-month written room block review point allowing Group to adjust the block size up or down at the group rate. The contract only has weekly pickup reports starting 8 weeks out and a 30-day post-event report; there is no formal block review/resizing mechanism, and no room-block audit provision addressing miscoded rooms at brand-associate or business rates specifically (the audit clause covers pickup reports/charges only, not a guest-list-vs-registration-list comparison).
findings.cd_standard: The room block should be reviewed in writing at approximately 24 and 12 months out, allowing Group to adjust the block by a set percentage at the group rate, and Group should have a no-cost audit comparing the hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list, with miscoded rooms credited to pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing 24 months and again 12 months prior to arrival. At Group's discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to [X]% at each review at the group rate. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a Group representative or independently by a ConferenceDirect or Group representative, and any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group — including rooms booked at brand-associate or business rates — will be credited to Group's pickup.'

findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly conflates gratuity and service charge as the same 25% charge, gives Hotel sole discretion to retain the entire amount as revenue with no obligation to distribute any portion to staff, and fails to disclose the split between staff compensation and hotel revenue.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be separately defined with both percentages disclosed; gratuity should be fully distributed to staff, while service charge, as hotel revenue, should be disclosed as such rather than conflated with a tip.
findings.proposed_language: A gratuity of [X]% of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account and fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of [Y]% (combined not to exceed 25% unless otherwise agreed), plus applicable tax, is distinct from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains sole discretion to determine the allocation and distribution of any gratuity collected on behalf of Group, and the Hotel may retain such gratuity as Hotel revenue without obligation to distribute it to service staff.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date of 30 days prior to arrival exceeds CD's maximum of 21 days, and the footer states the entire block is released in full at cutoff rather than handled through the negotiated hold/refund/consultation process described in the body text, creating an inconsistency that favors the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: The cutoff date should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date of April 26, 2027.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the Block must be submitted no later than thirty (30) days prior to the arrival date of April 26, 2027, unless a later deadline is expressly agreed in writing by the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on late undisputed balances is 2% per month, compounded monthly, exceeding CD's cap of 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less. Additionally the dispute window is only 7 days, shorter than the standard, and there is no automatic-credit provision if the Hotel never sends a credit application, and the credit-denial fallback is a single 50% prepayment rather than the staged schedule CD prefers.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on late, undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; Group should have a real dispute window before finance charges apply; credit denial should trigger a staged deposit schedule (25%/25%/50%) rather than a single lump prepayment; and if Hotel never sends a credit application, credit should be extended automatically.
findings.proposed_language: Any amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date shall accrue a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, on the outstanding, undisputed balance. Group shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of each invoice to dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit approval cannot be granted, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event. If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application, or fails to send a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group.
findings.quoted_text: Any amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date shall accrue a monthly finance charge of two percent (2%) per month on the outstanding balance, compounded monthly, until paid in full.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel disclaims any warranty or representation regarding current construction/renovation plans and their impact on Group's use of the facilities, contrary to CD's position that the Hotel should represent it has no current renovation plans and promise that future work will not interfere with Group's event. The notice period for confirmed future renovation is also only 14 days (versus CD's 30 days), and there is no provision addressing new-build/reopening scenarios with an operational date commitment.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent it has no current renovation plans affecting the group's space, promise that future work will not interfere with the group's use, and give 30 days' written notice, with damages coverage if a new-build's opening date changes.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. Hotel promises that any such construction or remodeling will not interfere with Group's use of the Hotel. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's notice.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no warranty, representation, or undertaking with respect to any construction, renovation, alteration, or other work that may be planned or under way at the Hotel during the event dates.

findings.finding_text: The Hotel expressly disclaims any obligation to give advance notice of collective bargaining agreement expiration or of labor disputes, and although Group may cancel within 30 days of a disruption, the clause explicitly states that any such cancellation does not relieve Group of financial obligations, room charges, or F&B minimums — meaning Group has no true no-liability cancellation right at all in a labor dispute scenario.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of disputes; if a strike, lockout, or expired contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability whatsoever.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, or no later than [date], Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability of any kind, including without liability for room charges, food and beverage minimums, or other fees.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any such cancellation right, the occurrence of any labor dispute or labor-related disruption at the Hotel shall not relieve Group of any financial obligation, payment requirement, or other liability under this Agreement, including but not limited to room charges, food and beverage minimums, and any other fees or charges incurred by or on behalf of Group.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are based on 'average daily room rate' rather than 70% of the single net group rate applied against the room block less allowable attrition, which is a materially different (and likely higher, since it isn't discounted to lost-profit basis explicitly at 70% of rate x block) calculation basis than CD's standard. Additionally, the rebooking credit only covers a 1-year window (CD allows for a longer negotiated period) and Group forfeits rebooking credit if the new event is booked below market rate, an extra condition not in CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Damages should be calculated as 70% of the single net group rate multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition (a lost-profit calculation), and the rebooking credit should not carry additional forfeiture conditions like a below-market-rate exclusion.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit, defined as seventy percent (70%) of Group's confirmed single net group rate at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition, on the sliding scale set forth in Exhibit A. Should Group rebook the Hotel for another meeting within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid, without regard to the rate at which the new event is booked.
findings.quoted_text: In the event Group cancels this Agreement, liquidated damages shall be assessed and calculated as a percentage of lost room profit based on the number of committed room nights that will not be occupied and the average daily room rate applicable to those nights.

findings.finding_text: The resale/mitigation clause is generally strong (diligent efforts, dollar-for-dollar credit, audit rights), but it does not specify that cancellation damages fall due only 30 days after the event and contingent on Hotel demonstrating its mitigation effort and that space went unsold — payment timing is instead governed by the separate cancellation clause without this contingency.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should not fall due until 30 days after the event, and only once the hotel demonstrates evidence of mitigation effort and that the rooms/space went unsold.
findings.proposed_language: Add to Section 5 or 4: 'Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.'
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall undertake diligent and good faith efforts to resell any Guest Rooms and function space released by Group pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause identifying specific function rooms, minimum square footage, ceiling heights, complimentary meeting space with rental waived, or in-room equipment (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC) commitments.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage and ceiling height, prohibit changes without written consent, provide complimentary meeting space with rental waived, and include a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge in each room.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Exhibit [X], with room rental charges waived, specifying each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.'

findings.finding_text: There is no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially reduces restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, contracted meeting space, or staffing ratios during the event.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes or limits facilities by more than 25% or materially reduces staffing ratios, it should offer equal alternatives at its own expense, and Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate if no resolution is reached within 30 days.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity, or materially reduces guest-to-staff service ratios, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability or the parties may modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.'

findings.finding_text: The room rate for the 2027 event appears already confirmed at $372, so a future-rate-cap clause may be less critical here; however, the contract does not address what happens if rates were to be revised or extended (e.g., for later add-on years), and there is no rate-decline protection or cap language present at all.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, the contract should cap any increase at 2% per year and provide for a decrease if market/published rates decline, fixing final rates no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.'

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no minimum staffing/server or bartender ratios for food and beverage functions, nor any cap on labor fees for small functions.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server and bartender staffing ratios at F&B functions with no labor fee for meeting them, except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees.'

findings.finding_text: There is no clause addressing AV or internet bandwidth quotes, discounts on additional needs, or a prohibition on tying discounted/complimentary internet to use of an in-house AV provider.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV and internet bandwidth quotes (minimum 10 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up), give a discount on later additions, and never condition discounted/complimentary internet on use of the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of provider. Hotel will honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, providing a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of [X]% on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.'

findings.finding_text: There is no provision on confirmation timelines, name changes at the group rate, individual room cancellation deadlines (6pm day of arrival), no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation confirmations should go out within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival); name changes should be allowed at the group rate up to arrival; individual cancellations should be free until 6pm day of arrival; no-shows should be reinstated the next night; and individual deposits should be refundable with 3 working days' notice.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if requested within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made at the group rate at any time up to arrival. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival.'

findings.finding_text: The complimentary room formula (1 per 40 paid rooms), forfeiture protection, and non-discretionary accrual match CD's position, but there is no mention that miscoded rooms found in an audit or no-show/cancellation fee room nights count toward the pickup used to calculate complimentary rooms, and no explicit statement about complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: All occupied rooms should count toward pickup including miscoded rooms found via audit and no-show/cancellation-fee room nights, and attendees should receive complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty-program status.
findings.proposed_language: Add: 'All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup for purposes of calculating complimentary rooms, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit. Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.'

analysis.document_notes: The contract does not include a commission clause for ConferenceDirect at all, nor a nondiscrimination clause; both are flagged as missing findings. No exhibit A text (cancellation damages schedule) was attached beyond the table shown, and no AV/internet quote exhibit is referenced or attached despite the AV/internet clause requiring one — this may exist as a separate exhibit not provided in this text. The document is well-organized with clear numbered sections; no illegible or structurally unusual portions were encountered.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, and liability is triggered at 85% pickup rather than CD's 70% threshold. The 100% occupancy credit provision is far narrower than CD's standard 95%-occupancy full credit. Damages are calculated against 'the applicable nightly rate' (average actual/projected rate) rather than the single confirmed net group rate, and there is no audit-formula guarantee (the clause even deems Group to have accepted Hotel's calculation if it fails to request records within 30 days), no F&B-to-attrition credit offset, and no rebate-on-rebooking credit.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be measured cumulatively across the entire block, triggered only below 70% of pickup, with 95%-or-higher occupancy on any night earning full credit, damages capped at 70% of lost profit on the single net group rate, audit rights for Group, and a credit-back if a CD client rebooks the hotel.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $279.00 (plus tax, if required by applicable law). For any night the Hotel achieves ninety-five percent (95%) occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. Hotel will provide Group's requested occupancy/city ledger records without a deemed-waiver deadline, and any excess F&B revenue above Group's minimum will be credited dollar-for-dollar against attrition damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis and applies to the total room nights committed by Group under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than 70% lost-profit on the net group rate, and the sliding-scale percentages in the table (68%/81%/90%) are dramatically higher than CD's standard tiers, with damages beginning at 20% for cancellations 180+ days out — far steeper than CD's approach. The narrative text and the table also conflict internally (narrative describes 20/40/60/80% tiers while the table shows 68/81/90%), creating ambiguity that favors the Hotel. Rebooking with the Hotel earns no automatic credit against damages (credit is at Hotel's sole discretion), contrary to CD's rebate-on-rebooking standard.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale calculated against 70% lost room profit on the single net group rate (not gross revenue) applied to the block less allowable attrition, with damages amounts disclosed, active resale mitigation, and a mandatory credit-back if a CD client rebooks.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit (defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $279.00, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition) on a sliding scale based on the date written cancellation notice is received, with each tier's dollar amount stated in this Agreement. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within [X] years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: If cancellation notice is provided one hundred eighty (180) days or more before the Event start date, liquidated damages shall equal twenty percent (20%) of gross room revenue.
findings.exposure_basis: Table shows damages up to 90% of gross room revenue on total block (465 rooms x 5 nights x $279 = $648,675 gross), substantially exceeding CD's 70%-of-lost-profit standard.

findings.finding_text: Section 5 explicitly denies Group any audit rights or access to the Hotel's resale records ('shall not be subject to disclosure to Group, audit by Group, or review by Group's representatives'), and does not tie cancellation damages payment to a 30-day-post-event window contingent on the Hotel demonstrating mitigation.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have a documented, verifiable mitigation duty, with records available to Group, and cancellation damages should not fall due until 30 days after the event and only once mitigation efforts are demonstrated.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation shall be made available to Group upon request for verification purposes. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation shall remain the sole property and responsibility of the Hotel and shall not be subject to disclosure to Group, audit by Group, or review by Group's representatives.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 40 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's maximum of 21 days. Post-cutoff, the hotel has no obligation to hold rooms and may reassign the block at its sole discretion, and the contract does not commit to honoring the group rate for as long as the hotel sells the same room type to the general public.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, with the group rate continuing post-cutoff for as long as the hotel sells rooms to the public (or the same room type once the block sells out), and unassigned rooms held, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any unassigned rooms in Group's block if Group pays for them in full, refunding those payments if later used by attendees, or, after consultation with Group, will release unassigned rooms to reduce Group's attrition liability. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type, or, once the block has sold, for as long as Hotel is selling the contracted room type to the public.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms in the Group block must be requested and confirmed with Hotel no later than forty (40) days prior to the first date of the Event, which shall be August 2, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure is limited to circumstances where performance has become 'physically impossible,' explicitly excluding commercial impracticability, inadvisability (including health/safety), or the 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger that CD's standard requires. It also excludes attendee safety concerns and unwillingness to travel absent an actual government order, and imposes a 10-day notice deadline from the triggering event (not present in CD's standard) as a condition of any refund, and deducts unspecified 'documented costs' from the refund.
findings.cd_standard: Either party should be able to cancel without liability when a qualifying cause makes performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including for health/safety reasons), or causes/leads Group to reasonably anticipate 20%+ attendee cancellations, with prompt full refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including epidemics, disease, government travel advisories, terrorism, and similar causes — in that party's reasonable judgment make it commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including from a health or safety standpoint), illegal, or impossible to perform, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel their attendance. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments in full within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: provided that performance has become physically impossible as a direct result of such cause and not merely more difficult, costly, or inconvenient

findings.finding_text: Termination for cause is a unilateral right granted only to the Hotel ('may terminate...without cause upon written notice to the Group if the Hotel determines in its sole discretion...'), with no corresponding termination-for-cause right granted to Group covering pandemic determination, labor disputes, ownership change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, or discriminatory legislation as a consolidated right (though some appear piecemeal elsewhere).
findings.cd_standard: Group should have its own broad termination-for-cause right — covering force majeure, pandemic determination, labor disputes, ownership/brand change, renovation, facility reductions, convention center unavailability, and discriminatory legislation — separate from the cancellation damages schedule.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: force majeure; Group's determination that an epidemic, pandemic, or infectious disease outbreak affects its ability to hold the Event; a qualifying labor dispute; a material change in Hotel ownership, management, or brand; interfering renovation; uncured facility or service reductions; unavailability of a relied-upon convention center or overflow hotel; or discriminatory state/local legislation. None of the foregoing triggers the cancellation clause's liquidated-damages calculation.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may terminate this Agreement immediately and without cause upon written notice to the Group if the Hotel determines in its sole discretion that circumstances render performance impossible or commercially impracticable.

findings.finding_text: Any F&B shortfall must be paid dollar-for-dollar in full, rather than at CD's 35% of the shortfall. The 35% reference in the contract instead triggers a different, Hotel-discretion penalty/renegotiation right when the shortfall itself exceeds 35% of the minimum, which is a materially worse mechanism than CD's standard. There is also no provision counting affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Any F&B shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, not dollar-for-dollar, and F&B revenue from affiliates/exhibitors should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the Minimum F&B Commitment, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: Should the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the Minimum F&B Commitment, the Group shall be obligated to pay the Hotel a shortfall fee equal to the difference between the Minimum F&B Commitment and the actual charges incurred.

findings.finding_text: The service charge is confirmed at 22%, but neither the gratuity percentage nor confirmation that gratuity/service charge will not be added to meeting room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee is included in the contract.
findings.cd_standard: Both the gratuity and service-charge percentages should be confirmed in the contract, and neither should be added to meeting room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: The gratuity percentage applicable to food and beverage charges will be [X]%, confirmed in this Agreement alongside the twenty-two percent (22%) service charge. Neither gratuity nor service charge will be added to meeting room rental fees or to rented equipment that already carries a labor fee.
findings.quoted_text: the service charge of twenty-two percent (22%) is retained by the Hotel as facility revenue and is separate and distinct from any voluntary gratuity offered to service personnel

findings.finding_text: The contract allows the Hotel to introduce new fees and surcharges after execution at its sole discretion, without Group's written approval, binding Group as a 'modification' to the fee schedule — directly contrary to CD's standard requiring Group's written approval before any post-signature charge is provided or posted. There is also a mandatory $26/night resort fee with no waiver and no confirmation that resort-fee services will still be honored if waived, and no protection against early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.cd_standard: Any post-signature charge requires Group's written approval before being provided or posted; resort fees should be waived for attendees (with services still honored), and attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel wish to introduce any additional fee, surcharge, or service charge after execution of this Agreement, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to Group's master account or attendee folios. Hotel will waive the $26.00 nightly resort fee for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee's included services, and will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, nor checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in or departing after check-out.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel may, at its sole discretion and without prior notice to Group, introduce additional fees, surcharges, and service charges after this Agreement is executed, and all such charges shall be binding upon Group as modifications to the schedule of fees set forth herein.
findings.exposure_basis: $26/night resort fee x 465 rooms x 5 nights if not waived = $60,450 in potential attendee resort-fee exposure

findings.finding_text: The rate parity clause only prevents prospective harm (adjustments apply only to reservations made after the lower rate is discovered) rather than requiring retroactive rate matching for existing reservations or full block-inclusion of attendee bookings at the lower rate, and it does not address parity with other groups' rates within 7 days before/after the event dates.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel sells below the group's rate, the group's rate should be adjusted retroactively for existing reservations (or all attendee bookings should count in the block regardless of rate) while keeping commission/pickup credit; the group's rate should also be no higher than other groups' rates within 7 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel offer a lower guestroom rate during the Event dates, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, and will make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees, with commission and pickup credit unaffected. Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.
findings.quoted_text: Any rate adjustment or modification resulting from such discovery shall apply only to reservations made after the lower rate is identified and communicated to Group in writing, and shall not apply retroactively to any reservations confirmed prior to such identification.

findings.finding_text: The finance charge on late undisputed balances is set at 1.5% per month, above CD's 1% cap. Additionally, the prepayment requirement for Group without approved credit is left as 'the percentage...designated by the Hotel' with no defined staged schedule or ceiling, rather than CD's defined staged deposit schedule or a fixed percentage.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charges on late, undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less. If credit is denied, Group should pay a staged schedule (25%/25%/50%) rather than an open-ended, hotel-designated percentage.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group fail to pay any undisputed invoice balance in full by the due date, Hotel will assess a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less. Where Group has not been approved for credit terms, Group will remit twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the credit denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to pay any undisputed invoice balance in full by the due date specified on the invoice, the Hotel shall assess a finance charge of 1.5% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower

findings.finding_text: The relocation clause provides comparable/superior accommodations, complimentary transportation, and does not credit the relocated night toward Group's pickup, commission eligibility, or future rate negotiation, and explicitly denies any room upgrade or welcome amenity on return, contrary to CD's standard. There is also no per-room-night rebate to Group's master account, no do-not-walk list provision, no requirement to walk transient/other-group guests first, and no additional compensation trigger for walking 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak-night block.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive an upgrade and welcome amenity on return; Group should receive a per-room-night rebate and credit for the relocated night toward pickup/commission; a do-not-walk list should be honored, transient/other-group guests walked first, and additional compensation owed if 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak block are walked.
findings.proposed_language: Upon return to the Hotel, the relocated guest will receive upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity from the General Manager. Hotel will credit Group's master account $[X] for each night a guest is relocated, and each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable at the group rate. Hotel will contact Group in advance of any walk, will not walk Group's attendees before transient guests and other groups, and will honor a do-not-walk list of key attendees identified by Group. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: the relocated guest shall return to the Vantage Point Hotel and Convention Center in a standard room assignment of the original booked category, with no room upgrade, no complimentary amenities beyond those included in the original rate agreement, and no additional services or concessions as compensation for the relocation. The relocated night or nights shall not be credited toward Group's room pickup for purposes of calculating minimum room guarantees, commission eligibility, or future rate negotiation

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission clause at all — no commitment to pay ConferenceDirect a 10% commission on actualized room revenue, no timing for payment, no survival through management/brand change, and no commission on cancellation damages collected.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue (including out-of-block, miscoded, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation-credited nights) within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable/non-transferable, surviving brand/management change, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.finding_text: No future-rate-cap clause is present; although this contract's rates are already fixed at $279 for all nights, the standards library calls for this clause where any future-year rates are not yet confirmed. As no unconfirmed future rate exists here, this may not be directly applicable, but there is no mechanism for a market-rate decline benefiting Group.
findings.cd_standard: Where future rates are not yet confirmed, increases should be capped at 2%/year, group rate should decline if market/published rates decline, and rates should be fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should any room rates in this Agreement remain unconfirmed at signing, Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over quoted rates, and will lower Group's rate by the same percentage should the market average rate for comparable hotels, or Hotel's own published rate, decline prior to Group's arrival. Final rates will be confirmed in writing no later than twelve (12) months prior to arrival.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no minimum banquet staffing ratios (servers per guest count for plated/buffet meals, bartenders per guest count) and no cap on labor/service fees tied to meeting those ratios.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should guarantee minimum server and bartender staffing ratios at F&B functions with no extra labor/service fee for meeting them, and a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. Functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $[X], with no other special labor or service fees for Group functions.

findings.finding_text: No audio-visual or internet bandwidth clause is present in the contract, so there is no commitment to honor quoted AV/internet pricing, no minimum bandwidth guarantee, and no protection against tying discounted internet to use of the in-house AV provider.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV and internet quotes (minimum 10 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up), give a stated discount on later additions, and never condition discounted internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs. Hotel will provide a minimum internet bandwidth of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload at the quoted rate, with a discount of [X]% on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

findings.finding_text: Function space in Exhibit A is 'held on a tentative basis' pending signature and lists spaces without minimum square footage or ceiling height specifications, and there is no statement that room rental is waived or that changes require both parties' written consent, nor a commitment to complimentary microphone/podium/power/lighting/HVAC per room.
findings.cd_standard: Function space should be named with minimum square footage and ceiling height, changed only by mutual written consent, provided complimentary with rental waived, and each room should include a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space listed in Exhibit A, specifying minimum square footage and ceiling height for each room, with room rental charges waived. No change will be made to function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.
findings.quoted_text: The function space set out below is held on a tentative basis and will be confirmed upon Hotel's receipt of Group's signed agreement.
findings.location_section: Exhibit A — Function Space and Catering

findings.finding_text: There is no clause addressing the hotel closing or limiting restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, or reducing staffing ratios, and no remedy (cancellation or renegotiation) if such reductions are not resolved within 30 days.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes/limits facilities by more than 25% or reduces staffing ratios materially, it should first offer equal alternatives; if unresolved within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or materially reduces guest-to-staff service ratios for housekeeping, food and beverage, or similar services, Hotel will first offer equal alternative facilities or services at its own expense. If no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability, or the parties may modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no reservation-procedures clause addressing confirmation timing, name changes, individual cancellation windows, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund/credit-against-attrition terms.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation handling should include prompt confirmations, name changes at group rate up to arrival, cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement, and individual cancellation money credited against attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation within four (4) days of booking (two (2) business days inside 30 days of arrival). Name changes may be made at the group rate up to the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the existing rate unless Group directs otherwise. Individual reservation deposits will be refunded with three (3) working days' notice, and any individual cancellation money Hotel retains will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.finding_text: The named storm clause's cancellation right expires 72 hours before the event's opening day, which is a narrower window than a clause allowing cancellation as the storm approaches closer to the event; it also requires forecast landfall within 75 miles rather than a broader threat radius, and does not clearly address a storm forecast during the event dates themselves triggering cancellation of only the affected portion.
findings.cd_standard: A named-storm clause should allow cancellation when a storm is forecast to affect the property within 72 hours of any event date, without requiring the right to lapse before the storm's closest approach to the event.
findings.proposed_language: Group may cancel this Agreement, or the affected portion of the Event, at no penalty if a named storm as defined by the National Hurricane Center is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within seventy-two (72) hours of any Event date, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel, upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice.
findings.quoted_text: Group's right to cancel on account of a named storm shall expire upon the expiration of seventy-two (72) hours before the Event's opening day; if no cancellation notice is received by the Hotel prior to the expiration of such window, Group shall have no further right to cancel

analysis.document_notes: The Cancellation clause (Section 4) contains an internal contradiction: the narrative text describes a 20%/40%/60%/80% sliding scale tied to 180/120/60-day thresholds, while the accompanying table lists a different scale (68%/81%/90%) tied to 180/90/30-day thresholds, plus a purported no-liability window through 364-181 days. This inconsistency should be flagged to the property for clarification/correction regardless of the substantive finding recorded against it. Nondiscrimination clause was not located in the contract body; if intended to be included per CD standards, it appears entirely absent, but is not recorded as a finding here since it was not raised as a required-but-missing item beyond noting its absence. Insurance/indemnification, ADA, damage deposit, review/audit, assignment, labor disputes, brand/ownership change, governing law/venue, attendee data, rebates, exclusivity vendors, hotel cancellation, and construction/renovation clauses were reviewed and found to align with CD's standard positions."
